#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the #34 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$pol…

# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive

blocks.text:
**HANG REPRODUCED** (EXIT=124 = timeout). The script spins forever watching run 111: 518 polls, served bodies all `{"status":"in_progress"}` (running=1 → refresh) — but the budget NEVER fires!

Why doesn't the budget fire? Budget check: `elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]` — reached only when `running` is NOT > 0 and NOT (stall condition). Look at the current wedge logic:

```bash
wedge=""
if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
 last_running="$now"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
 wedge="no running job for ..."
elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
 wedge="still unfinished after ..."
fi
``

With running=1: first branch → refresh → NO budget check! The budget only fires when nothing is running. With the OLD broken stub (running always 0) the budget fired. With a HEALTHY stub (running=1), the budget branch is unreachable → **the watcher spins forever on a healthy-but-long child**. THIS IS A REAL BUG IN THE PR'S SCRIPT that the broken fixture was hiding! The reviewer's point proven even deeper: "The next change to the fixture would land with a fully green suite" — actually worse: fixing the fixture EXPOSES a budget deadlock: a healthy child that runs LONGER than the budget never triggers the self-heal because the budget check is only in the `elif` chain behind "no running job".

Wait — is that the intended semantics? Pre-PR script: budget fired unconditionally when expired. The PR restructured: running>0 → refresh; else stall check; else budget check. So with a job running continuously past the budget, the watcher NEVER self-heals — it just watches forever until the LEG ceiling kills it (the exact gh-172 "bare ceiling kill" this PR claims to fix, now for a different signature!). That's a genuine regression the reviewer didn't even flag explicitly — but it's implied by thread 1's "the positive path has zero coverage; the next change would land fully green".

Hmm wait — actually let me re-read: is that pre-existing on the PR head? Yes — current script on the branch. The #34 'self-heal' test passed only because the stub reported 0 running (broken fixture) → budget fired. With a correct fixture (running=1), the self-heal budget NEVER fires. The whole #34 test group is vacuous too!

So my transient-test timing design needs reconsidering, AND the script needs the budget check to be reachable regardless of running-jobs. Correct semantics:

- stall wedge: no running job for queue_stall → wedge (gh-172).
- budget wedge: total elapsed > budget → wedge (#34) — REGARDLESS of running jobs (a child exceeding ~2× historical duration is wedged by definition, even if "progressing").

So the budget check must not be shadowed by the refresh branch. Restructure:

```bash
wedge=""
if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
 wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
 last_running="$now"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
 wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"

Why doesn't the budget fire? Budget check: `elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]` — reached only when `running` is NOT > 0 and NOT (stall condition). Look at the current wedge logic:

```bash
wedge=""
if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
 last_running="$now"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
 wedge="no running job for ..."
elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
 wedge="still unfinished after ..."
fi
``

With running=1: first branch → refresh → NO budget check! The budget only fires when nothing is running. With the OLD broken stub (running always 0) the budget fired. With a HEALTHY stub (running=1), the budget branch is unreachable → **the watcher spins forever on a healthy-but-long child**. THIS IS A REAL BUG IN THE PR'S SCRIPT that the broken fixture was hiding! The reviewer's point proven even deeper: "The next change to the fixture would land with a fully green suite" — actually worse: fixing the fixture EXPOSES a budget deadlock: a healthy child that runs LONGER than the budget never triggers the self-heal because the budget check is only in the `elif` chain behind "no running job".

Wait — is that the intended semantics? Pre-PR script: budget fired unconditionally when expired. The PR restructured: running>0 → refresh; else stall check; else budget check. So with a job running continuously past the budget, the watcher NEVER self-heals — it just watches forever until the LEG ceiling kills it (the exact gh-172 "bare ceiling kill" this PR claims to fix, now for a different signature!). That's a genuine regression the reviewer didn't even flag explicitly — but it's implied by thread 1's "the positive path has zero coverage; the next change would land fully green".

Hmm wait — actually let me re-read: is that pre-existing on the PR head? Yes — current script on the branch. The #34 'self-heal' test passed only because the stub reported 0 running (broken fixture) → budget fired. With a correct fixture (running=1), the self-heal budget NEVER fires. The whole #34 test group is vacuous too!

- stall wedge: no running job for queue_stall → wedge (gh-172).
- budget wedge: total elapsed > budget → wedge (#34) — REGARDLESS of running jobs (a child exceeding ~2× historical duration is wedged by definition, even if "progressing").

{"newText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi","oldText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"","path":"scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh"}

  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the

{"newText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi","oldText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress

Why doesn't the budget fire? Budget check: `elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]` — reached only when `running` is NOT > 0 and NOT (stall condition). Look at the current wedge logic:

```bash
wedge=""
if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
 last_running="$now"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
 wedge="no running job for ..."
elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
 wedge="still unfinished after ..."
fi
``

With running=1: first branch → refresh → NO budget check! The budget only fires when nothing is running. With the OLD broken stub (running always 0) the budget fired. With a HEALTHY stub (running=1), the budget branch is unreachable → **the watcher spins forever on a healthy-but-long child**. THIS IS A REAL BUG IN THE PR'S SCRIPT that the broken fixture was hiding! The reviewer's point proven even deeper: "The next change to the fixture would land with a fully green suite" — actually worse: fixing the fixture EXPOSES a budget deadlock: a healthy child that runs LONGER than the budget never triggers the self-heal because the budget check is only in the `elif` chain behind "no running job".

Wait — is that the intended semantics? Pre-PR script: budget fired unconditionally when expired. The PR restructured: running>0 → refresh; else stall check; else budget check. So with a job running continuously past the budget, the watcher NEVER self-heals — it just watches forever until the LEG ceiling kills it (the exact gh-172 "bare ceiling kill" this PR claims to fix, now for a different signature!). {"newText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi","oldText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"","path":"scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh"}

blocks.text:
Key clue: `sleep: invalid time interval ''`. The script now calls `sleep "$poll"` where poll is EMPTY?! Why? — because I introduced `poll` as the variable name for the API response, SHADOWING the `poll` knob (`poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"`)! The watch loop's `sleep "$poll"` now sleeps an empty string → sleep errors → and `set -euo pipefail` makes... actually `sleep` failing inside the loop → script exits with error (set -e) → exit 1 everywhere.

Classic variable collision. Rename my response variable: `poll` → `view` or `poll_out`. Use `snapshot` or `status_running`... Let me rename to `view` — hmm `view` is also a subcommand name but as a variable it's fine. Better: `poll_result`? Or `observed`. I'll use `poll_data`... Actually clean and descriptive: `status_running`? It holds "status/conclusion running". I'll go with `observed`.

Lines to change:
```bash
   observed="$(gh run view ...) || observed=""
   status="${observed%% *}"
   running="${observed##* }"
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
``

Also — the 'double-wedge'/'queue-stall' failures: dispatch count 1 vs 2 — because sleep broke the first attempt loop → exited before re-dispatch. And transient failure probably sleep too.

wedge=""
if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then

elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then

``

THIS IS A REAL BUG IN THE PR'S SCRIPT that the broken fixture was hiding! The reviewer's point proven even deeper: "The next change to the fixture would land with a fully green suite" — actually worse: fixing the fixture EXPOSES a budget deadlock: a healthy child that runs LONGER than the budget never triggers the self-heal because the budget check is only in the `elif` chain behind "no running job".

That's a genuine regression the reviewer didn't even flag explicitly — but it's implied by thread 1's "the positive path has zero coverage; the next change would land fully green".

{"newText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi","oldText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"","path":"scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh"}

blocks.text:
Key clue: `sleep: invalid time interval ''`. The script now calls `sleep "$poll"` where poll is EMPTY?! Why? — because I introduced `poll` as the variable name for the API response, SHADOWING the `poll` knob (`poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"`)! The watch loop's `sleep "$poll"` now sleeps an empty string → sleep errors → and `set -euo pipefail` makes... actually `sleep` failing inside the loop → script exits with error (set -e) → exit 1 everywhere.

Classic variable collision. Rename my response variable: `poll` → `view` or `poll_out`. Use `snapshot` or `status_running`... Let me rename to `view` — hmm `view` is also a subcommand name but as a variable it's fine. Better: `poll_result`? Or `observed`. I'll use `poll_data`... Actually clean and descriptive: `status_running`? It holds "status/conclusion running". I'll go with `observed`.

Lines to change:
```bash
   observed="$(gh run view ...) || observed=""
   status="${observed%% *}"
   running="${observed##* }"
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
``

Also — the 'double-wedge'/'queue-stall' failures: dispatch count 1 vs 2 — because sleep broke the first attempt loop → exited before re-dispatch. And transient failure probably sleep too.

{"newText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time

# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi","oldText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress

if [ "${args[$j]}" = "--json" ] && [[ "${args[$((j + 1))]}" == *jobs* ]]; then is_jobs=1; fi
        done
        if [ -f "$GH_STUB_DIR/cancelled-$id" ]; then
          status=completed; conclusion=cancelled; jobs_body=""
        else
          f="$GH_STUB_DIR/view-$id.txt"
          line=$(head -1 "$f")
          sed -i.bak '1d' "$f" && rm -f "$f.bak"
          if ! [ -s "$f" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$line" > "$f"; fi
          status="${line%% *}"; conclusion="${line#* }"
          jobs_body=""
          if [ "$is_jobs" = "1" ]; then
            jf="$GH_STUB_DIR/jobs-$id.txt"
            if [ -f "$jf" ]; then
              n=$(head -1 "$jf")
              sed -i.bak '1d' "$jf" && rm -f "$jf.bak"
              if ! [ -s "$jf" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$n" > "$jf"; fi
            else
              n=1
            fi
            jobs_body=$(seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
          fi
        fi
        if [ "$is_jobs" = "1" ]; then
          printf '%s\n' "$jobs_body" >> "$GH_STUB_DIR/jobs-served-$id.log"
          printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s","jobs":[%s]}' "$status" "$conclusion" "$jobs_body" | apply_jq
        else
          printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s"}' "$status" "$conclusion" | apply_jq

```bash
wedge=""

{"newText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi","oldText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"","path":"scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh"}

```bash
wedge=""
if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
 last_running="$now"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
 wedge="no running job for ..."
elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
 wedge="still unfinished after ..."
fi
``

With running=1: first branch → refresh → NO budget check! The budget only fires when nothing is running. With the OLD broken stub (running always 0) the budget fired. With a HEALTHY stub (running=1), the budget branch is unreachable → **the watcher spins forever on a healthy-but-long child**. THIS IS A REAL BUG IN THE PR'S SCRIPT that the broken fixture was hiding! The reviewer's point proven even deeper: "The next change to the fixture would land with a fully green suite" — actually worse: fixing the fixture EXPOSES a budget deadlock: a healthy child that runs LONGER than the budget never triggers the self-heal because the budget check is only in the `elif` chain behind "no running job".

Wait — is that the intended semantics? Pre-PR script: budget fired unconditionally when expired. The PR restructured: running>0 → refresh; else stall check; else budget check. So with a job running continuously past the budget, the watcher NEVER self-heals — it just watches forever until the LEG ceiling kills it (the exact gh-172 "bare ceiling kill" this PR claims to fix, now for a different signature!). That's a genuine regression the reviewer didn't even flag explicitly — but it's implied by thread 1's "the positive path has zero coverage; the next change would land fully green".

- stall wedge: no running job for queue_stall → wedge (gh-172).
- budget wedge: total elapsed > budget → wedge (#34) — REGARDLESS of running jobs (a child exceeding ~2× historical duration is wedged by definition, even if "progressing").

So the budget check must not be shadowed by the refresh branch. Restructure:

```bash
wedge=""
if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
 wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
 last_running="$now"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then

blocks.text:
**HANG REPRODUCED** (EXIT=124 = timeout). The script spins forever watching run 111: 518 polls, served bodies all `{"status":"in_progress"}` (running=1 → refresh) — but the budget NEVER fires!

Why doesn't the budget fire? Budget check: `elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]` — reached only when `running` is NOT > 0 and NOT (stall condition). Look at the current wedge logic:

```bash
wedge=""
if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
 last_running="$now"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
 wedge="no running job for ..."
elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
 wedge="still unfinished after ..."
fi
``

With running=1: first branch → refresh → NO budget check! The budget only fires when nothing is running. With the OLD broken stub (running always 0) the budget fired. With a HEALTHY stub (running=1), the budget branch is unreachable → **the watcher spins forever on a healthy-but-long child**. THIS IS A REAL BUG IN THE PR'S SCRIPT that the broken fixture was hiding! The reviewer's point proven even deeper: "The next change to the fixture would land with a fully green suite" — actually worse: fixing the fixture EXPOSES a budget deadlock: a healthy child that runs LONGER than the budget never triggers the self-heal because the budget check is only in the `elif` chain behind "no running job".

Wait — is that the intended semantics? Pre-PR script: budget fired unconditionally when expired. The PR restructured: running>0 → refresh; else stall check; else budget check. So with a job running continuously past the budget, the watcher NEVER self-heals — it just watches forever until the LEG ceiling kills it (the exact gh-172 "bare ceiling kill" this PR claims to fix, now for a different signature!). That's a genuine regression the reviewer didn't even flag explicitly — but it's implied by thread 1's "the positive path has zero coverage; the next change would land fully green".

Hmm wait — actually let me re-read: is that pre-existing on the PR head? Yes — current script on the branch. The #34 'self-heal' test passed only because the stub reported 0 running (broken fixture) → budget fired. With a correct fixture (running=1), the self-heal budget NEVER fires. The whole #34 test group is vacuous too!

So my transient-test timing design needs reconsidering, AND the script needs the budget check to be reachable regardless of running-jobs. Correct semantics:

- stall wedge: no running job for queue_stall → wedge (gh-172).
- budget wedge: total elapsed > budget → wedge (#34) — REGARDLESS of running jobs (a child exceeding ~2× historical duration is wedged by definition, even if "progressing").

So the budget check must not be shadowed by the refresh branch. Restructure:

```bash
wedge=""
if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
 wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
 last_running="$now"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
 wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"

{"newText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi","oldText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress

{"newText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi","oldText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress

Why doesn't the budget fire? Budget check: `elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]` — reached only when `running` is NOT > 0 and NOT (stall condition). Look at the current wedge logic:

```bash
wedge=""
if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
 last_running="$now"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
 wedge="no running job for ..."
elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
 wedge="still unfinished after ..."
fi
``

With running=1: first branch → refresh → NO budget check! The budget only fires when nothing is running. With the OLD broken stub (running always 0) the budget fired. With a HEALTHY stub (running=1), the budget branch is unreachable → **the watcher spins forever on a healthy-but-long child**. THIS IS A REAL BUG IN THE PR'S SCRIPT that the broken fixture was hiding! The reviewer's point proven even deeper: "The next change to the fixture would land with a fully green suite" — actually worse: fixing the fixture EXPOSES a budget deadlock: a healthy child that runs LONGER than the budget never triggers the self-heal because the budget check is only in the `elif` chain behind "no running job".

Wait — is that the intended semantics? Pre-PR script: budget fired unconditionally when expired. The PR restructured: running>0 → refresh; else stall check; else budget check. So with a job running continuously past the budget, the watcher NEVER self-heals — it just watches forever until the LEG ceiling kills it (the exact gh-172 "bare ceiling kill" this PR claims to fix, now for a different signature!). That's a genuine regression the reviewer didn't even flag explicitly — but it's implied by thread 1's "the positive path has zero coverage; the next change would land fully green".

Hmm wait — actually let me re-read: is that pre-existing on the PR head? Yes — current script on the branch. The #34 'self-heal' test passed only because the stub reported 0 running (broken fixture) → budget fired. With a correct fixture (running=1), the self-heal budget NEVER fires. The whole #34 test group is vacuous too!

So my transient-test timing design needs reconsidering, AND the script needs the budget check to be reachable regardless of running-jobs. Correct semantics:

- stall wedge: no running job for queue_stall → wedge (gh-172).
- budget wedge: total elapsed > budget → wedge (#34) — REGARDLESS of running jobs (a child exceeding ~2× historical duration is wedged by definition, even if "progressing").

So the budget check must not be shadowed by the refresh branch. Restructure:

```bash
wedge=""
if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
 wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
 last_running="$now"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
 wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
fi
``

Budget first (absolute), then refresh, then stall. This restores #34 semantics exactly (budget fires on expiry no matter what) and keeps the gh-172 stall.

{"newText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi","oldText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress

messages.preview: **Hang root-caused — this is a real bug the inert fixture was hiding.** With a *live* jobs feed (`running=1`), the PR's wedge chain refreshes `last_running` and the `elif`-chained **budget check becom…

blocks.text:
**HANG REPRODUCED** (EXIT=124 = timeout). The script spins forever watching run 111: 518 polls, served bodies all `{"status":"in_progress"}` (running=1 → refresh) — but the budget NEVER fires!

Why doesn't the budget fire? Budget check: `elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]` — reached only when `running` is NOT > 0 and NOT (stall condition). Look at the current wedge logic:

```bash
wedge=""
if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
 last_running="$now"
elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
 wedge="no running job for ..."
elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
 wedge="still unfinished after ..."
fi
``

With running=1: first branch → refresh → NO budget check! The budget only fires when nothing is running. With the OLD broken stub (running always 0) the budget fired. With a HEALTHY stub (running=1), the budget branch is unreachable → **the watcher spins forever on a healthy-but-long child**. {"newText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi","oldText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress

# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.

{"newText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi","oldText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress

{"newText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge —
# the 2026-10-20 TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time
# watching a re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted
# worker and then died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
#
# The window CANNOT distinguish a zombie-held pool from a healthy child
# queued behind a SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner macOS pool
# (testflight's build-ios/submit-ios and cli's build-macos matrix contend
# for the same fa-m5-1; one cli matrix leg can hold it for ~150m — and a
# hosted-runner queue crunch does the same to the play/website/addin
# children), so the default is scaled off the watch budget:
# max(600, budget/8). Long-budget legs wait out realistic sibling
# occupancy (testflight 15000s → ~31m) before wedging a quiet-but-alive
# child; short-budget legs keep the fast 10-minute zombie trip.
# Accepted residual class: a sibling occupancy longer than budget/8 can
# still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed damage
# inside the leg ceiling beats the gh-172 silent full-budget burn.
# DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS overrides (test shims).
if [ -n "${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}" ]; then
  queue_stall="$DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS"
else
  queue_stall=$(( budget / 8 > 600 ? budget / 8 : 600 ))
fi","oldText":"# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress

-# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way, and
-# the child is cancelled on the fail path so an orphaned queued run can
-# never publish unattended when the pool revives. gh-172 review: the
-# window is NOT a fixed 600s — it defaults to max(600, budget/8) because
-# a healthy child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the shared
-# single-runner pool shows the same "nothing running" signature for hours
-# (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on the one fa-m5-1 runner).
+# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way. The
+# window defaults to max(600, budget/8) so a healthy child queued behind a
+# SIBLING leg's job on the shared single-runner pool is not false-wedged
+# (the window cannot tell zombie-held from legitimately busy — see the
+# queue_stall comment below).
-# max(600, budget/8) — gh-172 no-running-job wedge window, scaled off the
-# leg budget so a busy shared pool is not mistaken for a zombie; gh-172
-# review), DW_DUMP_KNOBS (1 = print the effective knobs and exit — test
-# shim).
+# max(600, budget/8) — gh-172: no-running-job wedge window).
-# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
-# gh-172 review: a FIXED window cannot tell a zombie-held pool from a
-# legitimately busy one — the same "nothing in_progress" signature is
-# produced by a HEALTHY child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the
-# shared single-runner pool (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on
-# fa-m5-1 and can hold it for hours; a testflight child legitimately
-# shows nothing running all that time). The default therefore scales off
-# the leg budget: max(600, budget/8). Accepted residual class: contention
-# outliving the window but not the budget still self-heals (cancel + one
-# re-dispatch into a possibly-busy pool) — the second-wedge arithmetic
-# (2×(~10m version + window) + cancel wait) fits every leg ceiling with
-# the scaled windows, and the budget itself remains the backstop for long
-# legitimate waits.

# PR #1723 rework — all 3 open review threads fixed in code

## Issues/Notes

- **CI**: no failed checks at rework start (`ci_failures.md` — all checks green, no owned-violations table). Nothing to dispute; the work below addresses the review threads.
- **Open threads**: 3 (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 1 SUGGESTION) — each fixed with a code change, each with one reply under `outputs/review_replies/` (`thread_1.md`, `thread_2.md`, `thread_3.md`), indexed by `outputs/review_replies.json` (verbatim `threadId` + `inReplyToId` from `pr_discussions_raw.json`).
- **New bug found while fixing the BLOCKING thread** (the fixture inertness was hiding it): with a *live* jobs feed, the PR's `elif` chain made the **budget check unreachable** (it sat behind the running-job refresh branch), so the watcher spun **forever** on a healthy child that outlived the budget — reproduced at 500+ polls with no self-heal. The #344 budget self-heal only ever fired because the broken stub always reported 0 running jobs. Fixed: the budget check is evaluated **first**; the gh-172 stall check remains the fast path for the quiet zombie.
- Standing ops note from the PR unchanged: the physical `fa-m5-1` worker still needs reboot/de-register; the guard only bounds leg damage and surfaces the signature in the leg log.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 (BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub, vacuous transient test)** — TDD:
  - *RED*: kept the broken `seq -f` body construction while adding the new assertions — 3 tests failed exactly as the reviewer predicted (served bodies `['', …]`, no refresh coverage).
  - *GREEN*: stub body built with the suggested pipeline — `seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -` (`n=0` → `{"jobs":[]}`); the stub now appends the **body it actually served** to `jobs-served-<id>.log`, and the tests assert it — an inert fixture can never pass again. The "absent file = 1 job always running" contract is now true **and asserted**.
  - The transient test is re-timed so the refresh path is genuinely exercised: poll 1 quiet (3s) → poll 2 **running** (3s) → poll 3 quiet → poll 4 completes, window 5s, budget 60. Poll 3 stays under the window **only** if poll 2 refreshed `last_running`. *Mutation-verified*: disabling `last_running="$now"` turns the test red (`exit 0` → `exit 1`, cancel + re-dispatch in the log); the reviewer's "green with a deliberately broken guard" repro is dead.
- **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT — fixed 600s window false-wedges sibling-queued children)** — options (b)+(c):
  - Default is now `max(600, budget/8)` when `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` is unset (testflight 15000s → 1875s ≈ 31m; addin 3600s → 600s floor).
  - The effective window is echoed on the `watching …` line (`(queue-stall window Ns)`) for leg-log diagnostics, and pinned by a new test: floor (`800` → `600s`), scaled (`16000` → `2000s`); the queue-stall test asserts the explicit override still wins (`queue-stall window 1s`).
  - The false "A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the real contention analysis (cli `build-macos` matrix vs testflight's pinned jobs on `fa-m5-1`; hosted queue crunches), and the **accepted residual class** (sibling occupancy > budget/8 can still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed, inside the leg ceiling) is documented in the script header + `queue_stall` comment.
  - `daily-publish.yml` gh-172 arithmetic updated: second-wedge fail-fast worst case testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m stall = 294m < 360m.
- **Thread 3 (SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` per poll)**: the watch loop issues a single `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call; status/conclusion and the running count parse from one jq line (`… + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)`). Halves per-poll traffic and makes the two-call completion race structurally impossible; a failed call still counts as progress (blip tolerance preserved). The stub serves the combined call from `view-<id>.txt` + `jobs-<id>.txt` consumed in lockstep, still piping through the **real jq expression**, and the transient test pins **4 `run view` invocations for 4 polls** (the two-call shape made 8).

## Files Modified

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — budget-first wedge ordering (+ the bug comment); merged single `gh run view` call per poll; `queue_stall` default `max(600, budget/8)` with honest contention/residual-class docs; window echoed on the `watching` line; header + env-knob docs updated.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — stub: combined-call serving, corrected body construction, `jobs-served-<id>.log`; `DwRun.dir` + `servedJobs()` helper; new derivation test (floor/scaled/override); transient test rewritten (live-fixture assertion, refresh-exercising timing, no-cancel and single-call-per-poll assertions); override assertion added to the queue-stall test.
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — gh-172 comment: scaled window (1875s ≈ 31m for the 15000s testflight budget) and corrected second-wedge arithmetic (294m < 360m).

Pushed as `7cc7ff57cf` on `ai/gh-1722` (merge superseding the two intermediate origin auto-save snapshots `be81fba9`/`b07616c5` — partial shapes of the same rework, superseded by this completed, tested tree).

## Test Coverage

- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 22 tests, all green (was 21): new `stall window defaults to max(600, budget/8)…` test (floor + scaled + absent-file contract); rewritten transient test (live fixture, refresh mutation-coverage, no-cancel, one call per poll); override assertion on the queue-stall test.
- Mutation checks (reviewer's methodology): `last_running="$now"` disabled → transient test **red**; `seq -f`-style inert body → served-body assertions **red** (demonstrated in the RED phase).
- **Full suite**: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` → **11377 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed** (SUITE_EXIT=0) — the PR's baseline (11376) + 1 net new test, zero regressions.

{"content":"# PR #1723 rework — all 3 open review threads fixed in code

## Issues/Notes

- **CI**: no failed checks at rework start (`ci_failures.md` — all checks green, no owned-violations table). Nothing to dispute; the work below addresses the review threads.
- **Open threads**: 3 (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 1 SUGGESTION) — each fixed with a code change, each with one reply under `outputs/review_replies/` (`thread_1.md`, `thread_2.md`, `thread_3.md`), indexed by `outputs/review_replies.json` (verbatim `threadId` + `inReplyToId` from `pr_discussions_raw.json`).
- **New bug found while fixing the BLOCKING thread** (the fixture inertness was hiding it): with a *live* jobs feed, the PR's `elif` chain made the **budget check unreachable** (it sat behind the running-job refresh branch), so the watcher spun **forever** on a healthy child that outlived the budget — reproduced at 500+ polls with no self-heal. The #344 budget self-heal only ever fired because the broken stub always reported 0 running jobs. Fixed: the budget check is evaluated **first**; the gh-172 stall check remains the fast path for the quiet zombie.
- Standing ops note from the PR unchanged: the physical `fa-m5-1` worker still needs reboot/de-register; the guard only bounds leg damage and surfaces the signature in the leg log.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 (BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub, vacuous transient test)** — TDD:
  - *RED*: kept the broken `seq -f` body construction while adding the new assertions — 3 tests failed exactly as the reviewer predicted (served bodies `['', …]`, no refresh coverage).
  - *GREEN*: stub body built with the suggested pipeline — `seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -` (`n=0` → `{"jobs":[]}`); the stub now appends the **body it actually served** to `jobs-served-<id>.log`, and the tests assert it — an inert fixture can never pass again. The "absent file = 1 job always running" contract is now true **and asserted**.
  - The transient test is re-timed so the refresh path is genuinely exercised: poll 1 quiet (3s) → poll 2 **running** (3s) → poll 3 quiet → poll 4 completes, window 5s, budget 60. Poll 3 stays under the window **only** if poll 2 refreshed `last_running`. *Mutation-verified*: disabling `last_running="$now"` turns the test red (`exit 0` → `exit 1`, cancel + re-dispatch in the log); the reviewer's "green with a deliberately broken guard" repro is dead.
- **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT — fixed 600s window false-wedges sibling-queued children)** — options (b)+(c):
  - Default is now `max(600, budget/8)` when `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` is unset (testflight 15000s → 1875s ≈ 31m; addin 3600s → 600s floor).
  - The effective window is echoed on the `watching …` line (`(queue-stall window Ns)`) for leg-log diagnostics, and pinned by a new test: floor (`800` → `600s`), scaled (`16000` → `2000s`); the queue-stall test asserts the explicit override still wins (`queue-stall window 1s`).
  - The false "A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the real contention analysis (cli `build-macos` matrix vs testflight's pinned jobs on `fa-m5-1`; hosted queue crunches), and the **accepted residual class** (sibling occupancy > budget/8 can still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed, inside the leg ceiling) is documented in the script header + `queue_stall` comment.
  - `daily-publish.yml` gh-172 arithmetic updated: second-wedge fail-fast worst case testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m stall = 294m < 360m.
- **Thread 3 (SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` per poll)**: the watch loop issues a single `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call; status/conclusion and the running count parse from one jq line (`… + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)`). Halves per-poll traffic and makes the two-call completion race structurally impossible; a failed call still counts as progress (blip tolerance preserved). The stub serves the combined call from `view-<id>.txt` + `jobs-<id>.txt` consumed in lockstep, still piping through the **real jq expression**, and the transient test pins **4 `run view` invocations for 4 polls** (the two-call shape made 8).

## Files Modified

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — budget-first wedge ordering (+ the bug comment); merged single `gh run view` call per poll; `queue_stall` default `max(600, budget/8)` with honest contention/residual-class docs; window echoed on the `watching` line; header + env-knob docs updated.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — stub: combined-call serving, corrected body construction, `jobs-served-<id>.log`; `DwRun.dir` + `servedJobs()` helper; new derivation test (floor/scaled/override); transient test rewritten (live-fixture assertion, refresh-exercising timing, no-cancel and single-call-per-poll assertions); override assertion added to the queue-stall test.
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — gh-172 comment: scaled window (1875s ≈ 31m for the 15000s testflight budget) and corrected second-wedge arithmetic (294m < 360m).

Pushed as `7cc7ff57cf` on `ai/gh-1722` (merge superseding the two intermediate origin auto-save snapshots `be81fba9`/`b07616c5` — partial shapes of the same rework, superseded by this completed, tested tree).

## Test Coverage

- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 22 tests, all green (was 21): new `stall window defaults to max(600, budget/8)…` test (floor + scaled + absent-file contract); rewritten transient test (live fixture, refresh mutation-coverage, no-cancel, one call per poll); override assertion on the queue-stall test.

The #344 budget self-heal only ever fired because the broken stub always reported 0 running jobs. Fixed: the budget check is evaluated **first**; the gh-172 stall check remains the fast path for the quiet zombie.
- Standing ops note from the PR unchanged: the physical `fa-m5-1` worker still needs reboot/de-register; the guard only bounds leg damage and surfaces the signature in the leg log.

The "absent file = 1 job always running" contract is now true **and asserted**.
  - The transient test is re-timed so the refresh path is genuinely exercised: poll 1 quiet (3s) → poll 2 **running** (3s) → poll 3 quiet → poll 4 completes, window 5s, budget 60. Poll 3 stays under the window **only** if poll 2 refreshed `last_running`. *Mutation-verified*: disabling `last_running="$now"` turns the test red (`exit 0` → `exit 1`, cancel + re-dispatch in the log); the reviewer's "green with a deliberately broken guard" repro is dead.
- **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT — fixed 600s window false-wedges sibling-queued children)** — options (b)+(c):
  - Default is now `max(600, budget/8)` when `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` is unset (testflight 15000s → 1875s ≈ 31m; addin 3600s → 600s floor).

The "absent file = 1 job always running" contract is now true **and asserted**.
  - The transient test is re-timed so the refresh path is genuinely exercised: poll 1 quiet (3s) → poll 2 **running** (3s) → poll 3 quiet → poll 4 completes, window 5s, budget 60. Poll 3 stays under the window **only** if poll 2 refreshed `last_running`. *Mutation-verified*: disabling `last_running="$now"` turns the test red (`exit 0` → `exit 1`, cancel + re-dispatch in the log); the reviewer's "green with a deliberately broken guard" repro is dead.
- **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT — fixed 600s window false-wedges sibling-queued children)** — options (b)+(c):
  - Default is now `max(600, budget/8)` when `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` is unset (testflight 15000s → 1875s ≈ 31m; addin 3600s → 600s floor).
  - The effective window is echoed on the `watching …` line (`(queue-stall window Ns)`) for leg-log diagnostics, and pinned by a new test: floor (`800` → `600s`), scaled (`16000` → `2000s`); the queue-stall test asserts the explicit override still wins (`queue-stall window 1s`).
  - The false "A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the real contention analysis (cli `build-macos` matrix vs testflight's pinned jobs on `fa-m5-1`; hosted queue crunches), and the **accepted residual class** (sibling occupancy > budget/8 can still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed, inside the leg ceiling) is documented in the script header + `queue_stall` comment.
  - `daily-publish.yml` gh-172 arithmetic updated: second-wedge fail-fast worst case testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m stall = 294m < 360m.
- **Thread 3 (SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` per poll)**: the watch loop issues a single `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call; status/conclusion and the running count parse from one jq line (`… + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)`). Halves per-poll traffic and makes the two-call completion race structurally impossible; a failed call still counts as progress (blip tolerance preserved). The stub serves the combined call from `view-<id>.txt` + `jobs-<id>.txt` consumed in lockstep, still piping through the **real jq expression**, and the transient test pins **4 `run view` invocations for 4 polls** (the two-call shape made 8).

{"content":"# PR #1723 rework — all 3 open review threads fixed in code

## Issues/Notes

- **CI**: no failed checks at rework start (`ci_failures.md` — all checks green, no owned-violations table). Nothing to dispute; the work below addresses the review threads.
- **Open threads**: 3 (1 BLOCKING, 1 IMPORTANT, 1 SUGGESTION) — each fixed with a code change, each with one reply under `outputs/review_replies/` (`thread_1.md`, `thread_2.md`, `thread_3.md`), indexed by `outputs/review_replies.json` (verbatim `threadId` + `inReplyToId` from `pr_discussions_raw.json`).
- **New bug found while fixing the BLOCKING thread** (the fixture inertness was hiding it): with a *live* jobs feed, the PR's `elif` chain made the **budget check unreachable** (it sat behind the running-job refresh branch), so the watcher spun **forever** on a healthy child that outlived the budget — reproduced at 500+ polls with no self-heal. The #344 budget self-heal only ever fired because the broken stub always reported 0 running jobs. Fixed: the budget check is evaluated **first**; the gh-172 stall check remains the fast path for the quiet zombie.
- Standing ops note from the PR unchanged: the physical `fa-m5-1` worker still needs reboot/de-register; the guard only bounds leg damage and surfaces the signature in the leg log.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 (BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub, vacuous transient test)** — TDD:
  - *RED*: kept the broken `seq -f` body construction while adding the new assertions — 3 tests failed exactly as the reviewer predicted (served bodies `['', …]`, no refresh coverage).
  - *GREEN*: stub body built with the suggested pipeline — `seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -` (`n=0` → `{"jobs":[]}`); the stub now appends the **body it actually served** to `jobs-served-<id>.log`, and the tests assert it — an inert fixture can never pass again. The "absent file = 1 job always running" contract is now true **and asserted**.
  - The transient test is re-timed so the refresh path is genuinely exercised: poll 1 quiet (3s) → poll 2 **running** (3s) → poll 3 quiet → poll 4 completes, window 5s, budget 60. Poll 3 stays under the window **only** if poll 2 refreshed `last_running`. *Mutation-verified*: disabling `last_running="$now"` turns the test red (`exit 0` → `exit 1`, cancel + re-dispatch in the log); the reviewer's "green with a deliberately broken guard" repro is dead.
- **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT — fixed 600s window false-wedges sibling-queued children)** — options (b)+(c):
  - Default is now `max(600, budget/8)` when `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` is unset (testflight 15000s → 1875s ≈ 31m; addin 3600s → 600s floor).
  - The effective window is echoed on the `watching …` line (`(queue-stall window Ns)`) for leg-log diagnostics, and pinned by a new test: floor (`800` → `600s`), scaled (`16000` → `2000s`); the queue-stall test asserts the explicit override still wins (`queue-stall window 1s`).
  - The false "A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the real contention analysis (cli `build-macos` matrix vs testflight's pinned jobs on `fa-m5-1`; hosted queue crunches), and the **accepted residual class** (sibling occupancy > budget/8 can still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed, inside the leg ceiling) is documented in the script header + `queue_stall` comment.
  - `daily-publish.yml` gh-172 arithmetic updated: second-wedge fail-fast worst case testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m stall = 294m < 360m.
- **Thread 3 (SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` per poll)**: the watch loop issues a single `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call; status/conclusion and the running count parse from one jq line (`… + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)`). Halves per-poll traffic and makes the two-call completion race structurally impossible; a failed call still counts as progress (blip tolerance preserved). The stub serves the combined call from `view-<id>.txt` + `jobs-<id>.txt` consumed in lockstep, still piping through the **real jq expression**, and the transient test pins **4 `run view` invocations for 4 polls** (the two-call shape made 8).

## Files Modified

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — budget-first wedge ordering (+ the bug comment); merged single `gh run view` call per poll; `queue_stall` default `max(600, budget/8)` with honest contention/residual-class docs; window echoed on the `watching` line; header + env-knob docs updated.

- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — gh-172 comment: scaled window (1875s ≈ 31m for the 15000s testflight budget) and corrected second-wedge arithmetic (294m < 360m).

Pushed as `7cc7ff57cf` on `ai/gh-1722` (merge superseding the two intermediate origin auto-save snapshots `be81fba9`/`b07616c5` — partial shapes of the same rework, superseded by this completed, tested tree).

{"content":"# PR #1723 rework — all 3 open review threads fixed in code

## Issues/Notes

- **CI**: no failed checks at rework start (`ci_failures.md` — all checks green, no owned-violations table). Nothing to dispute; the work below addresses the review threads.

- **New bug found while fixing the BLOCKING thread** (the fixture inertness was hiding it): with a *live* jobs feed, the PR's `elif` chain made the **budget check unreachable** (it sat behind the running-job refresh branch), so the watcher spun **forever** on a healthy child that outlived the budget — reproduced at 500+ polls with no self-heal. The #344 budget self-heal only ever fired because the broken stub always reported 0 running jobs. Fixed: the budget check is evaluated **first**; the gh-172 stall check remains the fast path for the quiet zombie.
- Standing ops note from the PR unchanged: the physical `fa-m5-1` worker still needs reboot/de-register; the guard only bounds leg damage and surfaces the signature in the leg log.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 (BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub, vacuous transient test)** — TDD:
  - *RED*: kept the broken `seq -f` body construction while adding the new assertions — 3 tests failed exactly as the reviewer predicted (served bodies `['', …]`, no refresh coverage).
  - *GREEN*: stub body built with the suggested pipeline — `seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -` (`n=0` → `{"jobs":[]}`); the stub now appends the **body it actually served** to `jobs-served-<id>.log`, and the tests assert it — an inert fixture can never pass again. The "absent file = 1 job always running" contract is now true **and asserted**.
  - The transient test is re-timed so the refresh path is genuinely exercised: poll 1 quiet (3s) → poll 2 **running** (3s) → poll 3 quiet → poll 4 completes, window 5s, budget 60. Poll 3 stays under the window **only** if poll 2 refreshed `last_running`. *Mutation-verified*: disabling `last_running="$now"` turns the test red (`exit 0` → `exit 1`, cancel + re-dispatch in the log); the reviewer's "green with a deliberately broken guard" repro is dead.
- **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT — fixed 600s window false-wedges sibling-queued children)** — options (b)+(c):
  - Default is now `max(600, budget/8)` when `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` is unset (testflight 15000s → 1875s ≈ 31m; addin 3600s → 600s floor).
  - The effective window is echoed on the `watching …` line (`(queue-stall window Ns)`) for leg-log diagnostics, and pinned by a new test: floor (`800` → `600s`), scaled (`16000` → `2000s`); the queue-stall test asserts the explicit override still wins (`queue-stall window 1s`).
  - The false "A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the real contention analysis (cli `build-macos` matrix vs testflight's pinned jobs on `fa-m5-1`; hosted queue crunches), and the **accepted residual class** (sibling occupancy > budget/8 can still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed, inside the leg ceiling) is documented in the script header + `queue_stall` comment.
  - `daily-publish.yml` gh-172 arithmetic updated: second-wedge fail-fast worst case testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m stall = 294m < 360m.
- **Thread 3 (SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` per poll)**: the watch loop issues a single `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call; status/conclusion and the running count parse from one jq line (`… + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)`). Halves per-poll traffic and makes the two-call completion race structurally impossible; a failed call still counts as progress (blip tolerance preserved). The stub serves the combined call from `view-<id>.txt` + `jobs-<id>.txt` consumed in lockstep, still piping through the **real jq expression**, and the transient test pins **4 `run view` invocations for 4 polls** (the two-call shape made 8).

## Files Modified

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — budget-first wedge ordering (+ the bug comment); merged single `gh run view` call per poll; `queue_stall` default `max(600, budget/8)` with honest contention/residual-class docs; window echoed on the `watching` line; header + env-knob docs updated.

- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — gh-172 comment: scaled window (1875s ≈ 31m for the 15000s testflight budget) and corrected second-wedge arithmetic (294m < 360m).

{"content":"💡→✅ **Done — one `gh run view` call per poll.**

The watch loop now issues a single combined call and parses both fields from one jq line (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`, watch loop):

```bash
observed="$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
  --jq '"\(.status)/" + (.conclusion // "-") + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)' 2>/dev/null)" || observed=""
status="${observed%% *}"
running="${observed##* }"
```

(One tweak vs the sketch: the jq emits `status/conclusion count` on a single line rather than two lines, so a plain `read`-free parse keeps the error path unambiguous.)

- Halves the per-poll API traffic (60s cadence for hours), as suggested.
- The two-call race (status says `in_progress`, jobs then reports 0 for a completed run, one stall-clock tick on a dead run) is structurally impossible.
- A failed call yields an **empty poll**, which counts as progress — the "never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip" tolerance is preserved unchanged.

The test stub now serves the combined call from `view-<id>.txt` + `jobs-<id>.txt` consumed in lockstep, still piping fixtures through the **real jq expression** the script passes, and the transient-gap test asserts exactly **4 `run view` invocations for 4 polls** (the two-call shape made 8) — so the merge is pinned, not incidental.
