## PR Description

Closes #1722
### Root Cause

The 2026-10-20 `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run ([39402285750](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39402285750)) sat `queued` forever: the hung self-hosted worker ignored its own 90m job ceiling (250m actual), never processed the watcher's `gh run cancel` either, and kept holding the single-runner pool. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` polls **run** status only — it saw `in_progress` throughout, burned the remaining ~107m of leg time on a child that could never start, and died as a bare timeout (hence "no failed-step log available"), leaving the orphan queued to publish unattended on pool revival.

### Fix

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`: added a job-level liveness guard — a not-completed run with **no job in `in_progress` for `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` (600s)** is a wedge and rides the existing one-shot self-heal (cancel + re-dispatch once, then fail fast naming the pool). The watcher now also cancels the child on the fail path so a server-side-dead run can never publish unattended when the pool revives. A second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg (testflight ≈ 273m < 360m ceiling).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).
- Ops: cancelled the orphaned queued run `39402285750` (the containment the fixed watcher performs).

### Test Coverage

- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — `gh-172` group: pool-held child (alive, nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, fails fast with the pool signature on attempt 2, cancels the orphan; plus a transient between-jobs pickup gap that must NOT trip the guard. New stub fixture (`jobs-<id>.txt`) models `gh run view --json jobs`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **11376 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table is untouched.
- The physical `fa-m5-1` worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage and makes the signature visible in the leg log.

Poll 3 stays under the window **only** if poll 2 refreshed `last_running`. *Mutation-verified*: disabling `last_running="$now"` turns the test red (`exit 0` → `exit 1`, cancel + re-dispatch in the log); the reviewer's "green with a deliberately broken guard" repro is dead.

  - Default is now `max(600, budget/8)` when `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` is unset (testflight 15000s → 1875s ≈ 31m; addin 3600s → 600s floor).

Closes #1722

The 2026-10-20 `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run ([39402285750](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39402285750)) sat `queued` forever: the hung self-hosted worker ignored its own 90m job ceiling (250m actual), never processed the watcher's `gh run cancel` either, and kept holding the single-runner pool. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` polls **run** status only — it saw `in_progress` throughout, burned the remaining ~107m of leg time on a child that could never start, and died as a bare timeout (hence "no failed-step log available"), leaving the orphan queued to publish unattended on pool revival.

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`: added a job-level liveness guard — a not-completed run with **no job in `in_progress` for `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` (600s)** is a wedge and rides the existing one-shot self-heal (cancel + re-dispatch once, then fail fast naming the pool). The watcher now also cancels the child on the fail path so a server-side-dead run can never publish unattended when the pool revives. A second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg (testflight ≈ 273m < 360m ceiling).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).
- Ops: cancelled the orphaned queued run `39402285750` (the containment the fixed watcher performs).

New stub fixture (`jobs-<id>.txt`) models `gh run view --json jobs`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **11376 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.

- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table is untouched.
- The physical `fa-m5-1` worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage and makes the signature visible in the leg log.

**Finding**: An error poll (empty `observed`) sets `running=""`, which skips BOTH the refresh branch and the stall branch — so `last_running` stays at the last *successful* poll and the stall clock keeps accumulating during an API outage. Also the comment "counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip" overstates — it's "neither refreshes nor trips".

Reviewer offers two tightenings, either alone suffices:
(a) refresh `last_running="$now"` on error polls too ("cannot observe = cannot judge"), and/or
(b) reword the comment to match the accepted-residual-class framing.

While it says "no urgency — fold into a follow-up or leave as documented debt", the rework rules say every open thread needs a code fix in this pass. Best response: implement (a) — it's the materially safer behavior (an unobservable API period should not accumulate stall debt) AND (b) fix the comment to be accurate. Note the subtlety: with (a), during an outage the budget check still fires (budget is independent) — correct, the budget remains the backstop. 

Where exactly: in the error branch:

```bash
if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
 status="error/-"
 running=""
fi
``

But careful: `now=$(date +%s)` is computed AFTER the completed-check, and the refresh uses `$now`. The error branch runs BEFORE `now` exists for this iteration. Options: refresh with the timestamp captured later — restructure: move the error handling after `now=$(date +%s)`, or set a flag. Let me look at the current code:

```bash
   observed="$(gh run view ...)" || observed=""
   status="${observed%% *}"
   running="${observed##* }"
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     status="error/-"
     running=""

   if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
   now=$(date +%s)
   # comment...
   wedge=""

     wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
   elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then

``

The "absent file = 1 job always running" contract is now true **and asserted**.

Poll 3 stays under the window **only** if poll 2 refreshed `last_running`. *Mutation-verified*: disabling `last_running="$now"` turns the test red (`exit 0` → `exit 1`, cancel + re-dispatch in the log); the reviewer's "green with a deliberately broken guard" repro is dead.

New lap: 1 open SUGESTION thread on my own pushed code (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh:158`):

**Finding**: An error poll (empty `observed`) sets `running=""`, which skips BOTH the refresh branch and the stall branch — so `last_running` stays at the last *successful* poll and the stall clock keeps accumulating during an API outage. A sustained outage (> stall window, ~31m on testflight) that starts while the child is quiet false-wedges a healthy child. Also the comment "counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip" overstates — it's "neither refreshes nor trips".

Reviewer offers two tightenings, either alone suffices:
(a) refresh `last_running="$now"` on error polls too ("cannot observe = cannot judge"), and/or
(b) reword the comment to match the accepted-residual-class framing.

While it says "no urgency — fold into a follow-up or leave as documented debt", the rework rules say every open thread needs a code fix in this pass. Best response: implement (a) — it's the materially safer behavior (an unobservable API period should not accumulate stall debt) AND (b) fix the comment to be accurate. Note the subtlety: with (a), during an outage the budget check still fires (budget is independent) — correct, the budget remains the backstop. 

Where exactly: in the error branch:

```bash
if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
 status="error/-"
 running=""
fi
``

But careful: `now=$(date +%s)` is computed AFTER the completed-check, and the refresh uses `$now`. The error branch runs BEFORE `now` exists for this iteration. Options: refresh with the timestamp captured later — restructure: move the error handling after `now=$(date +%s)`, or set a flag. Let me look at the current code:

```bash
   observed="$(gh run view ...)" || observed=""
   status="${observed%% *}"
   running="${observed##* }"
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     status="error/-"
     running=""
   fi
   if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
   now=$(date +%s)
   # comment...
   wedge=""
   if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
     wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
   elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
     last_running="$now"
   elif ...
``

Simplest correct change: in the error branch, don't have `now` yet — but `date +%s` is cheap; I can set `now=$(date +%s)` inside the error branch before refreshing, and then the later `now=$(date +%s)` re-captures (fine, same second typically; slightly later is fine too). OR restructure: capture `now` right after the parse, before the completed check — but `now` is only needed when not completed; capturing always is harmless (one extra date call per poll — negligible vs the gh call). Cleanest: set `now=$(date +%s)` BEFORE the completed check? That changes the semantic slightly (now includes the view-call duration — already does). Actually simplest minimal diff honoring the reviewer's snippet: inside the error branch:

```bash
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     # API unreachable — no signal, no stall accumulation (review: an
     # outage outliving the window must not false-wedge a healthy child;
     # the budget stays the backstop). Cannot observe = cannot judge.
     status="error/-"
     running=""
     last_running="$(date +%s)"
   fi
``

Wait — but then the comment block before the wedge chain mentions "An empty poll (failed call) counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip." — reword per (b): "A failed poll is 'cannot observe': it refreshes the stall clock (no signal, no accumulation) — an outage outliving the window is not treated as a child stall; the budget remains the backstop. (A single blip neither trips nor accumulates.)"

Hmm, one nuance: refreshing last_running on error polls means a MISBEHAVING gh (persistent failures) never trips the stall — only the budget catches it. That's exactly what the reviewer wants ("cannot observe = cannot judge", "the containment action is moot anyway: gh run cancel hits the same unavailable API"). ✓

TDD: RED test — a test where the stub's view calls fail for a stretch LONGER than the stall window while the child is quiet... but "quiet" (running=0) can't be observed if ALL view calls fail. The false-wedge scenario: last successful poll saw running=0 (clock started), then N failed polls spanning > window, then a successful poll sees the child healthy (running=1 or completes). With CURRENT code: the stall check at the first post-outage successful poll: elapsed (now - last_running) > window → false wedge. With FIX: error polls refreshed the clock → no wedge.

Test design:
- DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3, DW_POLL_SECONDS=0 (fast spins; error polls spin rapidly — each failed call consumes nothing), budget must be > total time or exactly controlled.
- Stub needs an error-injection fixture: e.g. `view-error-calls` file containing a NUMBER of initial view calls to fail (exit 1 / empty output). Add stub support: if `$GH_STUB_DIR/view-fail-next` exists with count N > 0, decrement and exit 1 (empty output, like a real gh network failure). The script: `observed="" || ...` → error path.

- poll1 (success): view 'in_progress -', jobs '0' → running=0 → clock=last_running=t0. 
- polls 2..k (FAIL, 4+ seconds): each refreshes clock with fix; without fix, clock stays t0.
- poll k+1 (success): 'in_progress -', jobs '1' (running job! healthy child resumed) → with fix: running=1 → refresh, no wedge → continue → next poll completes success → exit 0. Without fix: running=1 → the elif chain: running>0 → REFRESH branch (no wedge check!!) — wait, if the post-outage poll reports running=1, the wedge never evaluates (running>0 refreshes) — NOT RED.

So: after the outage, the successful poll sees jobs '0' again, THEN the child picks up: next success poll sees '1', then completes. Without fix: wedge at the first post-outage quiet poll. With fix: no wedge; the quiet-post-outage poll's elapsed = 0 (clock just refreshed by the last error poll... wait — with the fix, the last error poll set last_running≈t_k; the first success poll at t_k(+ε): running=0 → elapsed ~0 < 3 ✓ no wedge; then jobs '1' → refresh; then completed → exit 0 ✓.

Error polls with sleep=0 spin fast (each ~ms) — thousands of polls in 3s — fine, but for the clock to EXCEED the window without the fix, real wall time must pass: the stretch of failed polls must last > 3s wall. Options: DW_POLL_SECONDS applies to `sleep $poll` at the END of the loop iteration — error polls DO sleep poll seconds each iteration (the sleep is at the bottom, unconditional). So DW_POLL_SECONDS=2 with, say, 3 failed polls → outage spans ~4-6s > 3 ✓. Then success poll. Total runtime ~6-8s. Margins: without fix, the post-outage success poll at t≈6: elapsed 6 > 3 ✓ wedge (RED, margin 3s). With fix: clock refreshed at t≈4 (last error poll), success poll t≈6: elapsed 2 < 3 ✓ no wedge (margin 1s) — acceptable; widen: poll=2, 4 failed polls (t≈8), stall=5: RED: 8 > 5 ✓ margin 3; GREEN: last error at t≈8, success at t≈8-10 → elapsed ≤2 < 5 ✓ margin 3. Then jobs '1' poll, then completed poll. Budget: 60 (never fires). Runtime ~12s (6 polls × 2s). Fine.

The #344 budget self-heal only ever fired because the broken stub always reported 0 running jobs. Fixed: the budget check is evaluated **first**; the gh-172 stall check remains the fast path for the quiet zombie.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 (BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub, vacuous transient test)** — TDD:
  - *RED*: kept the broken `seq -f` body construction while adding the new assertions — 3 tests failed exactly as the reviewer predicted (served bodies `['', …]`, no refresh coverage).

The "absent file = 1 job always running" contract is now true **and asserted**.
  - The transient test is re-timed so the refresh path is genuinely exercised: poll 1 quiet (3s) → poll 2 **running** (3s) → poll 3 quiet → poll 4 completes, window 5s, budget 60. Poll 3 stays under the window **only** if poll 2 refreshed `last_running`. *Mutation-verified*: disabling `last_running="$now"` turns the test red (`exit 0` → `exit 1`, cancel + re-dispatch in the log); the reviewer's "green with a deliberately broken guard" repro is dead.
- **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT — fixed 600s window false-wedges sibling-queued children)** — options (b)+(c):
  - Default is now `max(600, budget/8)` when `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` is unset (testflight 15000s → 1875s ≈ 31m; addin 3600s → 600s floor).
  - The effective window is echoed on the `watching …` line (`(queue-stall window Ns)`) for leg-log diagnostics, and pinned by a new test: floor (`800` → `600s`), scaled (`16000` → `2000s`); the queue-stall test asserts the explicit override still wins (`queue-stall window 1s`).
  - The false "A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the real contention analysis (cli `build-macos` matrix vs testflight's pinned jobs on `fa-m5-1`; hosted queue crunches), and the **accepted residual class** (sibling occupancy > budget/8 can still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed, inside the leg ceiling) is documented in the script header + `queue_stall` comment.
  - `daily-publish.yml` gh-172 arithmetic updated: second-wedge fail-fast worst case testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m stall = 294m < 360m.
- **Thread 3 (SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` per poll)**: the watch loop issues a single `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call; status/conclusion and the running count parse from one jq line (`… + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)`). Halves per-poll traffic and makes the two-call completion race structurally impossible; a failed call still counts as progress (blip tolerance preserved). The stub serves the combined call from `view-<id>.txt` + `jobs-<id>.txt` consumed in lockstep, still piping through the **real jq expression**, and the transient test pins **4 `run view` invocations for 4 polls** (the two-call shape made 8).

## PR Description

Closes #1722
### Root Cause

The 2026-10-20 `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run ([39402285750](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39402285750)) sat `queued` forever: the hung self-hosted worker ignored its own 90m job ceiling (250m actual), never processed the watcher's `gh run cancel` either, and kept holding the single-runner pool. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` polls **run** status only — it saw `in_progress` throughout, burned the remaining ~107m of leg time on a child that could never start, and died as a bare timeout (hence "no failed-step log available"), leaving the orphan queued to publish unattended on pool revival.

### Fix

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`: added a job-level liveness guard — a not-completed run with **no job in `in_progress` for `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` (600s)** is a wedge and rides the existing one-shot self-heal (cancel + re-dispatch once, then fail fast naming the pool). The watcher now also cancels the child on the fail path so a server-side-dead run can never publish unattended when the pool revives. A second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg (testflight ≈ 273m < 360m ceiling).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).
- Ops: cancelled the orphaned queued run `39402285750` (the containment the fixed watcher performs).

### Test Coverage

- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — `gh-172` group: pool-held child (alive, nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, fails fast with the pool signature on attempt 2, cancels the orphan; plus a transient between-jobs pickup gap that must NOT trip the guard. New stub fixture (`jobs-<id>.txt`) models `gh run view --json jobs`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **11376 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table is untouched.
- The physical `fa-m5-1` worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage and makes the signature visible in the leg log.

New lap: 1 open SUGESTION thread on my own pushed code (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh:158`):

**Finding**: An error poll (empty `observed`) sets `running=""`, which skips BOTH the refresh branch and the stall branch — so `last_running` stays at the last *successful* poll and the stall clock keeps accumulating during an API outage. A sustained outage (> stall window, ~31m on testflight) that starts while the child is quiet false-wedges a healthy child. Also the comment "counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip" overstates — it's "neither refreshes nor trips".

Reviewer offers two tightenings, either alone suffices:
(a) refresh `last_running="$now"` on error polls too ("cannot observe = cannot judge"), and/or
(b) reword the comment to match the accepted-residual-class framing.

While it says "no urgency — fold into a follow-up or leave as documented debt", the rework rules say every open thread needs a code fix in this pass. Best response: implement (a) — it's the materially safer behavior (an unobservable API period should not accumulate stall debt) AND (b) fix the comment to be accurate. Note the subtlety: with (a), during an outage the budget check still fires (budget is independent) — correct, the budget remains the backstop. 

Where exactly: in the error branch:

```bash
if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
 status="error/-"
 running=""
fi
``

But careful: `now=$(date +%s)` is computed AFTER the completed-check, and the refresh uses `$now`. The error branch runs BEFORE `now` exists for this iteration. Options: refresh with the timestamp captured later — restructure: move the error handling after `now=$(date +%s)`, or set a flag. Let me look at the current code:

```bash
   observed="$(gh run view ...)" || observed=""
   status="${observed%% *}"
   running="${observed##* }"
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     status="error/-"
     running=""
   fi
   if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
   now=$(date +%s)
   # comment...
   wedge=""
   if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
     wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
   elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
     last_running="$now"
   elif ...
``

Simplest correct change: in the error branch, don't have `now` yet — but `date +%s` is cheap; I can set `now=$(date +%s)` inside the error branch before refreshing, and then the later `now=$(date +%s)` re-captures (fine, same second typically; slightly later is fine too). OR restructure: capture `now` right after the parse, before the completed check — but `now` is only needed when not completed; capturing always is harmless (one extra date call per poll — negligible vs the gh call). Cleanest: set `now=$(date +%s)` BEFORE the completed check? That changes the semantic slightly (now includes the view-call duration — already does). Actually simplest minimal diff honoring the reviewer's snippet: inside the error branch:

```bash
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     # API unreachable — no signal, no stall accumulation (review: an
     # outage outliving the window must not false-wedge a healthy child;
     # the budget stays the backstop). Cannot observe = cannot judge.
     status="error/-"
     running=""
     last_running="$(date +%s)"
   fi
``

Wait — but then the comment block before the wedge chain mentions "An empty poll (failed call) counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip." — reword per (b): "A failed poll is 'cannot observe': it refreshes the stall clock (no signal, no accumulation) — an outage outliving the window is not treated as a child stall; the budget remains the backstop. (A single blip neither trips nor accumulates.)"

Hmm, one nuance: refreshing last_running on error polls means a MISBEHAVING gh (persistent failures) never trips the stall — only the budget catches it. That's exactly what the reviewer wants ("cannot observe = cannot judge", "the containment action is moot anyway: gh run cancel hits the same unavailable API"). ✓

TDD: RED test — a test where the stub's view calls fail for a stretch LONGER than the stall window while the child is quiet... but "quiet" (running=0) can't be observed if ALL view calls fail. The false-wedge scenario: last successful poll saw running=0 (clock started), then N failed polls spanning > window, then a successful poll sees the child healthy (running=1 or completes). With CURRENT code: the stall check at the first post-outage successful poll: elapsed (now - last_running) > window → false wedge. With FIX: error polls refreshed the clock → no wedge.

Test design:
- DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3, DW_POLL_SECONDS=0 (fast spins; error polls spin rapidly — each failed call consumes nothing), budget must be > total time or exactly controlled.
- Stub needs an error-injection fixture: e.g. `view-error-calls` file containing a NUMBER of initial view calls to fail (exit 1 / empty output). Add stub support: if `$GH_STUB_DIR/view-fail-next` exists with count N > 0, decrement and exit 1 (empty output, like a real gh network failure). The script: `observed="" || ...` → error path.

Timeline (poll=0, stall=3):
- poll1 (success): view 'in_progress -', jobs '0' → running=0 → clock=last_running=t0. 
- polls 2..k (FAIL, 4+ seconds): each refreshes clock with fix; without fix, clock stays t0.
- poll k+1 (success): 'in_progress -', jobs '1' (running job! healthy child resumed) → with fix: running=1 → refresh, no wedge → continue → next poll completes success → exit 0. Without fix: running=1 → the elif chain: running>0 → REFRESH branch (no wedge check!!) — wait, if the post-outage poll reports running=1, the wedge never evaluates (running>0 refreshes) — NOT RED.

Hmm. For the current code to false-wedge, the first successful poll after the outage must report running=0 AND elapsed > window: then `elif running==0 && elapsed > stall` → wedge. So: after the outage, the successful poll sees jobs '0' again, THEN the child picks up: next success poll sees '1', then completes. Without fix: wedge at the first post-outage quiet poll. With fix: no wedge; the quiet-post-outage poll's elapsed = 0 (clock just refreshed by the last error poll... wait — with the fix, the last error poll set last_running≈t_k; the first success poll at t_k(+ε): running=0 → elapsed ~0 < 3 ✓ no wedge; then jobs '1' → refresh; then completed → exit 0 ✓.

Timing: need the failed-poll stretch to span > stall (3s) for RED. Error polls with sleep=0 spin fast (each ~ms) — thousands of polls in 3s — fine, but for the clock to EXCEED the window without the fix, real wall time must pass: the stretch of failed polls must last > 3s wall. Options: DW_POLL_SECONDS applies to `sleep $poll` at the END of the loop iteration — error polls DO sleep poll seconds each iteration (the sleep is at the bottom, unconditional). So DW_POLL_SECONDS=2 with, say, 3 failed polls → outage spans ~4-6s > 3 ✓. Then success poll. Total runtime ~6-8s. Margins: without fix, the post-outage success poll at t≈6: elapsed 6 > 3 ✓ wedge (RED, margin 3s). With fix: clock refreshed at t≈4 (last error poll), success poll t≈6: elapsed 2 < 3 ✓ no wedge (margin 1s) — acceptable; widen: poll=2, 4 failed polls (t≈8), stall=5: RED: 8 > 5 ✓ margin 3; GREEN: last error at t≈8, success at t≈8-10 → elapsed ≤2 < 5 ✓ margin 3. Then jobs '1' poll, then completed poll. Budget: 60 (never fires). Runtime ~12s (6 polls × 2s). Fine.

Wait — also ensure the FIRST poll (before outage) is success+quiet: sets baseline clock. Fixtures: view-111: 'in_progress -' ×5 then 'completed success' (repeats last when exhausted). jobs-111: '0\n' (baseline), then error polls consume nothing (stub exits before serving), then '0\n' (post-outage quiet), '1\n' (running), then completed poll consumes whatever (last repeats). **Finding**: An error poll (empty `observed`) sets `running=""`, which skips BOTH the refresh branch and the stall branch — so `last_running` stays at the last *successful* poll and the stall clock keeps accumulating during an API outage. A sustained outage (> stall window, ~31m on testflight) that starts while the child is quiet false-wedges a healthy child. Also the comment "counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip" overstates — it's "neither refreshes nor trips".

Reviewer offers two tightenings, either alone suffices:
(a) refresh `last_running="$now"` on error polls too ("cannot observe = cannot judge"), and/or
(b) reword the comment to match the accepted-residual-class framing.

While it says "no urgency — fold into a follow-up or leave as documented debt", the rework rules say every open thread needs a code fix in this pass. Best response: implement (a) — it's the materially safer behavior (an unobservable API period should not accumulate stall debt) AND (b) fix the comment to be accurate. Note the subtlety: with (a), during an outage the budget check still fires (budget is independent) — correct, the budget remains the backstop. 

Where exactly: in the error branch:

```bash
if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
 status="error/-"
 running=""
fi
``

But careful: `now=$(date +%s)` is computed AFTER the completed-check, and the refresh uses `$now`. The error branch runs BEFORE `now` exists for this iteration. Options: refresh with the timestamp captured later — restructure: move the error handling after `now=$(date +%s)`, or set a flag. Let me look at the current code:

```bash
   observed="$(gh run view ...)" || observed=""
   status="${observed%% *}"
   running="${observed##* }"
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     status="error/-"
     running=""
   fi
   if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
   now=$(date +%s)
   # comment...
   wedge=""
   if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
     wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
   elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
     last_running="$now"
   elif ...
``

Simplest correct change: in the error branch, don't have `now` yet — but `date +%s` is cheap; I can set `now=$(date +%s)` inside the error branch before refreshing, and then the later `now=$(date +%s)` re-captures (fine, same second typically; slightly later is fine too). OR restructure: capture `now` right after the parse, before the completed check — but `now` is only needed when not completed; capturing always is harmless (one extra date call per poll — negligible vs the gh call). Cleanest: set `now=$(date +%s)` BEFORE the completed check? That changes the semantic slightly (now includes the view-call duration — already does). Actually simplest minimal diff honoring the reviewer's snippet: inside the error branch:

```bash
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     # API unreachable — no signal, no stall accumulation (review: an
     # outage outliving the window must not false-wedge a healthy child;
     # the budget stays the backstop). Cannot observe = cannot judge.
     status="error/-"

``

(A single blip neither trips nor accumulates.)"

Hmm, one nuance: refreshing last_running on error polls means a MISBEHAVING gh (persistent failures) never trips the stall — only the budget catches it. That's exactly what the reviewer wants ("cannot observe = cannot judge", "the containment action is moot anyway: gh run cancel hits the same unavailable API"). ✓

TDD: RED test — a test where the stub's view calls fail for a stretch LONGER than the stall window while the child is quiet... but "quiet" (running=0) can't be observed if ALL view calls fail. The false-wedge scenario: last successful poll saw running=0 (clock started), then N failed polls spanning > window, then a successful poll sees the child healthy (running=1 or completes). With CURRENT code: the stall check at the first post-outage successful poll: elapsed (now - last_running) > window → false wedge. With FIX: error polls refreshed the clock → no wedge.

The #344 budget self-heal only ever fired because the broken stub always reported 0 running jobs. Fixed: the budget check is evaluated **first**; the gh-172 stall check remains the fast path for the quiet zombie.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 (BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub, vacuous transient test)** — TDD:
  - *RED*: kept the broken `seq -f` body construction while adding the new assertions — 3 tests failed exactly as the reviewer predicted (served bodies `['', …]`, no refresh coverage).
  - *GREEN*: stub body built with the suggested pipeline — `seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -` (`n=0` → `{"jobs":[]}`); the stub now appends the **body it actually served** to `jobs-served-<id>.log`, and the tests assert it — an inert fixture can never pass again. The "absent file = 1 job always running" contract is now true **and asserted**.
  - The transient test is re-timed so the refresh path is genuinely exercised: poll 1 quiet (3s) → poll 2 **running** (3s) → poll 3 quiet → poll 4 completes, window 5s, budget 60. Poll 3 stays under the window **only** if poll 2 refreshed `last_running`. *Mutation-verified*: disabling `last_running="$now"` turns the test red (`exit 0` → `exit 1`, cancel + re-dispatch in the log); the reviewer's "green with a deliberately broken guard" repro is dead.
- **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT — fixed 600s window false-wedges sibling-queued children)** — options (b)+(c):
  - Default is now `max(600, budget/8)` when `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` is unset (testflight 15000s → 1875s ≈ 31m; addin 3600s → 600s floor).
  - The effective window is echoed on the `watching …` line (`(queue-stall window Ns)`) for leg-log diagnostics, and pinned by a new test: floor (`800` → `600s`), scaled (`16000` → `2000s`); the queue-stall test asserts the explicit override still wins (`queue-stall window 1s`).
  - The false "A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the real contention analysis (cli `build-macos` matrix vs testflight's pinned jobs on `fa-m5-1`; hosted queue crunches), and the **accepted residual class** (sibling occupancy > budget/8 can still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed, inside the leg ceiling) is documented in the script header + `queue_stall` comment.
  - `daily-publish.yml` gh-172 arithmetic updated: second-wedge fail-fast worst case testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m stall = 294m < 360m.
- **Thread 3 (SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` per poll)**: the watch loop issues a single `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call; status/conclusion and the running count parse from one jq line (`… + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)`). Halves per-poll traffic and makes the two-call completion race structurally impossible; a failed call still counts as progress (blip tolerance preserved). The stub serves the combined call from `view-<id>.txt` + `jobs-<id>.txt` consumed in lockstep, still piping through the **real jq expression**, and the transient test pins **4 `run view` invocations for 4 polls** (the two-call shape made 8).

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — budget-first wedge ordering (+ the bug comment); merged single `gh run view` call per poll; `queue_stall` default `max(600, budget/8)` with honest contention/residual-class docs; window echoed on the `watching` line; header + env-knob docs updated.

## PR Description

Closes #1722
### Root Cause

The 2026-10-20 `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run ([39402285750](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39402285750)) sat `queued` forever: the hung self-hosted worker ignored its own 90m job ceiling (250m actual), never processed the watcher's `gh run cancel` either, and kept holding the single-runner pool. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` polls **run** status only — it saw `in_progress` throughout, burned the remaining ~107m of leg time on a child that could never start, and died as a bare timeout (hence "no failed-step log available"), leaving the orphan queued to publish unattended on pool revival.

### Fix

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`: added a job-level liveness guard — a not-completed run with **no job in `in_progress` for `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` (600s)** is a wedge and rides the existing one-shot self-heal (cancel + re-dispatch once, then fail fast naming the pool). The watcher now also cancels the child on the fail path so a server-side-dead run can never publish unattended when the pool revives. A second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg (testflight ≈ 273m < 360m ceiling).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).
- Ops: cancelled the orphaned queued run `39402285750` (the containment the fixed watcher performs).

### Test Coverage

- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — `gh-172` group: pool-held child (alive, nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, fails fast with the pool signature on attempt 2, cancels the orphan; plus a transient between-jobs pickup gap that must NOT trip the guard. New stub fixture (`jobs-<id>.txt`) models `gh run view --json jobs`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **11376 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table is untouched.
- The physical `fa-m5-1` worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage and makes the signature visible in the leg log.

New lap: 1 open SUGESTION thread on my own pushed code (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh:158`):

**Finding**: An error poll (empty `observed`) sets `running=""`, which skips BOTH the refresh branch and the stall branch — so `last_running` stays at the last *successful* poll and the stall clock keeps accumulating during an API outage. A sustained outage (> stall window, ~31m on testflight) that starts while the child is quiet false-wedges a healthy child. Also the comment "counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip" overstates — it's "neither refreshes nor trips".

Reviewer offers two tightenings, either alone suffices:
(a) refresh `last_running="$now"` on error polls too ("cannot observe = cannot judge"), and/or
(b) reword the comment to match the accepted-residual-class framing.

While it says "no urgency — fold into a follow-up or leave as documented debt", the rework rules say every open thread needs a code fix in this pass. Best response: implement (a) — it's the materially safer behavior (an unobservable API period should not accumulate stall debt) AND (b) fix the comment to be accurate. Note the subtlety: with (a), during an outage the budget check still fires (budget is independent) — correct, the budget remains the backstop. 

Where exactly: in the error branch:

```bash
if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
 status="error/-"
 running=""
fi
``

But careful: `now=$(date +%s)` is computed AFTER the completed-check, and the refresh uses `$now`. The error branch runs BEFORE `now` exists for this iteration. Options: refresh with the timestamp captured later — restructure: move the error handling after `now=$(date +%s)`, or set a flag. Let me look at the current code:

```bash
   observed="$(gh run view ...)" || observed=""
   status="${observed%% *}"
   running="${observed##* }"
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     status="error/-"
     running=""
   fi
   if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
   now=$(date +%s)
   # comment...
   wedge=""
   if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
     wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
   elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
     last_running="$now"
   elif ...
``

Simplest correct change: in the error branch, don't have `now` yet — but `date +%s` is cheap; I can set `now=$(date +%s)` inside the error branch before refreshing, and then the later `now=$(date +%s)` re-captures (fine, same second typically; slightly later is fine too). OR restructure: capture `now` right after the parse, before the completed check — but `now` is only needed when not completed; capturing always is harmless (one extra date call per poll — negligible vs the gh call). Cleanest: set `now=$(date +%s)` BEFORE the completed check? That changes the semantic slightly (now includes the view-call duration — already does). Actually simplest minimal diff honoring the reviewer's snippet: inside the error branch:

```bash
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     # API unreachable — no signal, no stall accumulation (review: an
     # outage outliving the window must not false-wedge a healthy child;
     # the budget stays the backstop). Cannot observe = cannot judge.
     status="error/-"
     running=""
     last_running="$(date +%s)"
   fi
``

Wait — but then the comment block before the wedge chain mentions "An empty poll (failed call) counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip." — reword per (b): "A failed poll is 'cannot observe': it refreshes the stall clock (no signal, no accumulation) — an outage outliving the window is not treated as a child stall; the budget remains the backstop. (A single blip neither trips nor accumulates.)"

Hmm, one nuance: refreshing last_running on error polls means a MISBEHAVING gh (persistent failures) never trips the stall — only the budget catches it. That's exactly what the reviewer wants ("cannot observe = cannot judge", "the containment action is moot anyway: gh run cancel hits the same unavailable API"). ✓

TDD: RED test — a test where the stub's view calls fail for a stretch LONGER than the stall window while the child is quiet... but "quiet" (running=0) can't be observed if ALL view calls fail. The false-wedge scenario: last successful poll saw running=0 (clock started), then N failed polls spanning > window, then a successful poll sees the child healthy (running=1 or completes). With CURRENT code: the stall check at the first post-outage successful poll: elapsed (now - last_running) > window → false wedge. With FIX: error polls refreshed the clock → no wedge.

Test design:
- DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3, DW_POLL_SECONDS=0 (fast spins; error polls spin rapidly — each failed call consumes nothing), budget must be > total time or exactly controlled.
- Stub needs an error-injection fixture: e.g. `view-error-calls` file containing a NUMBER of initial view calls to fail (exit 1 / empty output). Add stub support: if `$GH_STUB_DIR/view-fail-next` exists with count N > 0, decrement and exit 1 (empty output, like a real gh network failure). The script: `observed="" || ...` → error path.

Timeline (poll=0, stall=3):
- poll1 (success): view 'in_progress -', jobs '0' → running=0 → clock=last_running=t0. 
- polls 2..k (FAIL, 4+ seconds): each refreshes clock with fix; without fix, clock stays t0.
- poll k+1 (success): 'in_progress -', jobs '1' (running job! healthy child resumed) → with fix: running=1 → refresh, no wedge → continue → next poll completes success → exit 0. Without fix: running=1 → the elif chain: running>0 → REFRESH branch (no wedge check!!) — wait, if the post-outage poll reports running=1, the wedge never evaluates (running>0 refreshes) — NOT RED.

Hmm. For the current code to false-wedge, the first successful poll after the outage must report running=0 AND elapsed > window: then `elif running==0 && elapsed > stall` → wedge. So: after the outage, the successful poll sees jobs '0' again, THEN the child picks up: next success poll sees '1', then completes. Without fix: wedge at the first post-outage quiet poll. With fix: no wedge; the quiet-post-outage poll's elapsed = 0 (clock just refreshed by the last error poll... wait — with the fix, the last error poll set last_running≈t_k; the first success poll at t_k(+ε): running=0 → elapsed ~0 < 3 ✓ no wedge; then jobs '1' → refresh; then completed → exit 0 ✓.

Timing: need the failed-poll stretch to span > stall (3s) for RED. Error polls with sleep=0 spin fast (each ~ms) — thousands of polls in 3s — fine, but for the clock to EXCEED the window without the fix, real wall time must pass: the stretch of failed polls must last > 3s wall. Options: DW_POLL_SECONDS applies to `sleep $poll` at the END of the loop iteration — error polls DO sleep poll seconds each iteration (the sleep is at the bottom, unconditional). So DW_POLL_SECONDS=2 with, say, 3 failed polls → outage spans ~4-6s > 3 ✓. Then success poll. Total runtime ~6-8s. Margins: without fix, the post-outage success poll at t≈6: elapsed 6 > 3 ✓ wedge (RED, margin 3s). With fix: clock refreshed at t≈4 (last error poll), success poll t≈6: elapsed 2 < 3 ✓ no wedge (margin 1s) — acceptable; widen: poll=2, 4 failed polls (t≈8), stall=5: RED: 8 > 5 ✓ margin 3; GREEN: last error at t≈8, success at t≈8-10 → elapsed ≤2 < 5 ✓ margin 3. Then jobs '1' poll, then completed poll. Budget: 60 (never fires). Runtime ~12s (6 polls × 2s). Fine.

Wait — also ensure the FIRST poll (before outage) is success+quiet: sets baseline clock. Fixtures: view-111: 'in_progress -' ×5 then 'completed success' (repeats last when exhausted). jobs-111: '0\n' (baseline), then error polls consume nothing (stub exits before serving), then '0\n' (post-outage quiet), '1\n' (running), then completed poll consumes whatever (last repeats). Let me count stub consumption: stub fails BEFORE touching fixtures when fail-next>0.

jobs file lines consumed per SUCCESS combined call: poll1→'0'; fail polls 2-5 (no consume); poll6→'0'; poll7→'1'; poll8 (completed)→ repeats '1'. jobs-111.txt = '0\n0\n1\n'.
view-111.txt: poll1→'in_progress -'; polls2-5 fail; poll6→'…

The reviewer offers: refresh `last_running` on error polls ("cannot observe = cannot judge") and/or reword the comment.

  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"

    # running-job count arrive atomically — half the per-poll traffic and
    # no race where the two calls straddle a completion and one iteration
    # ticks the stall clock on an already-dead run. An empty poll (failed

      --jq '"\(.status)/" + (.conclusion // "-") + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)' 2>/dev/null)" || observed=""

New lap: 1 open SUGESTION thread on my own pushed code (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh:158`):

**Finding**: An error poll (empty `observed`) sets `running=""`, which skips BOTH the refresh branch and the stall branch — so `last_running` stays at the last *successful* poll and the stall clock keeps accumulating during an API outage. A sustained outage (> stall window, ~31m on testflight) that starts while the child is quiet false-wedges a healthy child. Also the comment "counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip" overstates — it's "neither refreshes nor trips".

Reviewer offers two tightenings, either alone suffices:
(a) refresh `last_running="$now"` on error polls too ("cannot observe = cannot judge"), and/or
(b) reword the comment to match the accepted-residual-class framing.

While it says "no urgency — fold into a follow-up or leave as documented debt", the rework rules say every open thread needs a code fix in this pass. Best response: implement (a) — it's the materially safer behavior (an unobservable API period should not accumulate stall debt) AND (b) fix the comment to be accurate. Note the subtlety: with (a), during an outage the budget check still fires (budget is independent) — correct, the budget remains the backstop. 

Where exactly: in the error branch:

```bash
if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
 status="error/-"
 running=""
fi
``

But careful: `now=$(date +%s)` is computed AFTER the completed-check, and the refresh uses `$now`. The error branch runs BEFORE `now` exists for this iteration. Options: refresh with the timestamp captured later — restructure: move the error handling after `now=$(date +%s)`, or set a flag. Let me look at the current code:

```bash
   observed="$(gh run view ...)" || observed=""
   status="${observed%% *}"
   running="${observed##* }"
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     status="error/-"
     running=""
   fi
   if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
   now=$(date +%s)
   # comment...
   wedge=""
   if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
     wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
   elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
     last_running="$now"
   elif ...
``

Simplest correct change: in the error branch, don't have `now` yet — but `date +%s` is cheap; I can set `now=$(date +%s)` inside the error branch before refreshing, and then the later `now=$(date +%s)` re-captures (fine, same second typically; slightly later is fine too). OR restructure: capture `now` right after the parse, before the completed check — but `now` is only needed when not completed; capturing always is harmless (one extra date call per poll — negligible vs the gh call). Cleanest: set `now=$(date +%s)` BEFORE the completed check? That changes the semantic slightly (now includes the view-call duration — already does). Actually simplest minimal diff honoring the reviewer's snippet: inside the error branch:

```bash
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     # API unreachable — no signal, no stall accumulation (review: an
     # outage outliving the window must not false-wedge a healthy child;
     # the budget stays the backstop). Cannot observe = cannot judge.
     status="error/-"
     running=""
     last_running="$(date +%s)"
   fi
``

Wait — but then the comment block before the wedge chain mentions "An empty poll (failed call) counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip." — reword per (b): "A failed poll is 'cannot observe': it refreshes the stall clock (no signal, no accumulation) — an outage outliving the window is not treated as a child stall; the budget remains the backstop. (A single blip neither trips nor accumulates.)"

Hmm, one nuance: refreshing last_running on error polls means a MISBEHAVING gh (persistent failures) never trips the stall — only the budget catches it. That's exactly what the reviewer wants ("cannot observe = cannot judge", "the containment action is moot anyway: gh run cancel hits the same unavailable API"). ✓

TDD: RED test — a test where the stub's view calls fail for a stretch LONGER than the stall window while the child is quiet... but "quiet" (running=0) can't be observed if ALL view calls fail. The false-wedge scenario: last successful poll saw running=0 (clock started), then N failed polls spanning > window, then a successful poll sees the child healthy (running=1 or completes). With CURRENT code: the stall check at the first post-outage successful poll: elapsed (now - last_running) > window → false wedge. With FIX: error polls refreshed the clock → no wedge.

Test design:
- DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3, DW_POLL_SECONDS=0 (fast spins; error polls spin rapidly — each failed call consumes nothing), budget must be > total time or exactly controlled.
- Stub needs an error-injection fixture: e.g. `view-error-calls` file containing a NUMBER of initial view calls to fail (exit 1 / empty output). Add stub support: if `$GH_STUB_DIR/view-fail-next` exists with count N > 0, decrement and exit 1 (empty output, like a real gh network failure). The script: `observed="" || ...` → error path.

Timeline (poll=0, stall=3):
- poll1 (success): view 'in_progress -', jobs '0' → running=0 → clock=last_running=t0. 
- polls 2..k (FAIL, 4+ seconds): each refreshes clock with fix; without fix, clock stays t0.
- poll k+1 (success): 'in_progress -', jobs '1' (running job! healthy child resumed) → with fix: running=1 → refresh, no wedge → continue → next poll completes success → exit 0. Without fix: running=1 → the elif chain: running>0 → REFRESH branch (no wedge check!!) — wait, if the post-outage poll reports running=1, the wedge never evaluates (running>0 refreshes) — NOT RED.

Hmm. For the current code to false-wedge, the first successful poll after the outage must report running=0 AND elapsed > window: then `elif running==0 && elapsed > stall` → wedge. So: after the outage, the successful poll sees jobs '0' again, THEN the child picks up: next success poll sees '1', then completes. Without fix: wedge at the first post-outage quiet poll. With fix: no wedge; the quiet-post-outage poll's elapsed = 0 (clock just refreshed by the last error poll... wait — with the fix, the last error poll set last_running≈t_k; the first success poll at t_k(+ε): running=0 → elapsed ~0 < 3 ✓ no wedge; then jobs '1' → refresh; then completed → exit 0 ✓.

Timing: need the failed-poll stretch to span > stall (3s) for RED. Error polls with sleep=0 spin fast (each ~ms) — thousands of polls in 3s — fine, but for the clock to EXCEED the window without the fix, real wall time must pass: the stretch of failed polls must last > 3s wall. Options: DW_POLL_SECONDS applies to `sleep $poll` at the END of the loop iteration — error polls DO sleep poll seconds each iteration (the sleep is at the bottom, unconditional). So DW_POLL_SECONDS=2 with, say, 3 failed polls → outage spans ~4-6s > 3 ✓. Then success poll. Total runtime ~6-8s. Margins: without fix, the post-outage success poll at t≈6: elapsed 6 > 3 ✓ wedge (RED, margin 3s). With fix: clock refreshed at t≈4 (last error poll), success poll t≈6: elapsed 2 < 3 ✓ no wedge (margin 1s) — acceptable; widen: poll=2, 4 failed polls (t≈8), stall=5: RED: 8 > 5 ✓ margin 3; GREEN: last error at t≈8, success at t≈8-10 → elapsed ≤2 < 5 ✓ margin 3. Then jobs '1' poll, then completed poll. Budget: 60 (never fires). Runtime ~12s (6 polls × 2s). Fine.

Wait — also ensure the FIRST poll (before outage) is success+quiet: sets baseline clock.     # no race where the two calls straddle a completion and one iteration
    # ticks the stall clock on an already-dead run. An empty poll (failed

{"content":"# PR #1723 rework — all 3 open review threads fixed in code

## Issues/Notes

- **CI**: no failed checks at rework start (`ci_failures.md` — all checks green, no owned-violations table). Nothing to dispute; the work below addresses the review threads.

- **New bug found while fixing the BLOCKING thread** (the fixture inertness was hiding it): with a *live* jobs feed, the PR's `elif` chain made the **budget check unreachable** (it sat behind the running-job refresh branch), so the watcher spun **forever** on a healthy child that outlived the budget — reproduced at 500+ polls with no self-heal. The #344 budget self-heal only ever fired because the broken stub always reported 0 running jobs. Fixed: the budget check is evaluated **first**; the gh-172 stall check remains the fast path for the quiet zombie.
- Standing ops note from the PR unchanged: the physical `fa-m5-1` worker still needs reboot/de-register; the guard only bounds leg damage and surfaces the signature in the leg log.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 (BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub, vacuous transient test)** — TDD:
  - *RED*: kept the broken `seq -f` body construction while adding the new assertions — 3 tests failed exactly as the reviewer predicted (served bodies `['', …]`, no refresh coverage).
  - *GREEN*: stub body built with the suggested pipeline — `seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -` (`n=0` → `{"jobs":[]}`); the stub now appends the **body it actually served** to `jobs-served-<id>.log`, and the tests assert it — an inert fixture can never pass again. The "absent file = 1 job always running" contract is now true **and asserted**.
  - The transient test is re-timed so the refresh path is genuinely exercised: poll 1 quiet (3s) → poll 2 **running** (3s) → poll 3 quiet → poll 4 completes, window 5s, budget 60. Poll 3 stays under the window **only** if poll 2 refreshed `last_running`. *Mutation-verified*: disabling `last_running="$now"` turns the test red (`exit 0` → `exit 1`, cancel + re-dispatch in the log); the reviewer's "green with a deliberately broken guard" repro is dead.
- **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT — fixed 600s window false-wedges sibling-queued children)** — options (b)+(c):
  - Default is now `max(600, budget/8)` when `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` is unset (testflight 15000s → 1875s ≈ 31m; addin 3600s → 600s floor).
  - The effective window is echoed on the `watching …` line (`(queue-stall window Ns)`) for leg-log diagnostics, and pinned by a new test: floor (`800` → `600s`), scaled (`16000` → `2000s`); the queue-stall test asserts the explicit override still wins (`queue-stall window 1s`).
  - The false "A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the real contention analysis (cli `build-macos` matrix vs testflight's pinned jobs on `fa-m5-1`; hosted queue crunches), and the **accepted residual class** (sibling occupancy > budget/8 can still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed, inside the leg ceiling) is documented in the script header + `queue_stall` comment.
  - `daily-publish.yml` gh-172 arithmetic updated: second-wedge fail-fast worst case testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m stall = 294m < 360m.
- **Thread 3 (SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` per poll)**: the watch loop issues a single `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call; status/conclusion and the running count parse from one jq line (`… + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)`). Halves per-poll traffic and makes the two-call completion race structurally impossible; a failed call still counts as progress (blip tolerance preserved). The stub serves the combined call from `view-<id>.txt` + `jobs-<id>.txt` consumed in lockstep, still piping through the **real jq expression**, and the transient test pins **4 `run view` invocations for 4 polls** (the two-call shape made 8).

## Files Modified

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — budget-first wedge ordering (+ the bug comment); merged single `gh run view` call per poll; `queue_stall` default `max(600, budget/8)` with honest contention/residual-class docs; window echoed on the `watching` line; header + env-knob docs updated.

## PR Description

Closes #1722
### Root Cause

The 2026-10-20 `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run ([39402285750](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39402285750)) sat `queued` forever: the hung self-hosted worker ignored its own 90m job ceiling (250m actual), never processed the watcher's `gh run cancel` either, and kept holding the single-runner pool. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` polls **run** status only — it saw `in_progress` throughout, burned the remaining ~107m of leg time on a child that could never start, and died as a bare timeout (hence "no failed-step log available"), leaving the orphan queued to publish unattended on pool revival.

### Fix

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`: added a job-level liveness guard — a not-completed run with **no job in `in_progress` for `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` (600s)** is a wedge and rides the existing one-shot self-heal (cancel + re-dispatch once, then fail fast naming the pool). The watcher now also cancels the child on the fail path so a server-side-dead run can never publish unattended when the pool revives. A second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg (testflight ≈ 273m < 360m ceiling).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).
- Ops: cancelled the orphaned queued run `39402285750` (the containment the fixed watcher performs).

### Test Coverage

- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — `gh-172` group: pool-held child (alive, nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, fails fast with the pool signature on attempt 2, cancels the orphan; plus a transient between-jobs pickup gap that must NOT trip the guard. New stub fixture (`jobs-<id>.txt`) models `gh run view --json jobs`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **11376 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table is untouched.
- The physical `fa-m5-1` worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage and makes the signature visible in the leg log.

New lap: 1 open SUGESTION thread on my own pushed code (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh:158`):

**Finding**: An error poll (empty `observed`) sets `running=""`, which skips BOTH the refresh branch and the stall branch — so `last_running` stays at the last *successful* poll and the stall clock keeps accumulating during an API outage. A sustained outage (> stall window, ~31m on testflight) that starts while the child is quiet false-wedges a healthy child. Also the comment "counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip" overstates — it's "neither refreshes nor trips".

Reviewer offers two tightenings, either alone suffices:
(a) refresh `last_running="$now"` on error polls too ("cannot observe = cannot judge"), and/or
(b) reword the comment to match the accepted-residual-class framing.

While it says "no urgency — fold into a follow-up or leave as documented debt", the rework rules say every open thread needs a code fix in this pass. Best response: implement (a) — it's the materially safer behavior (an unobservable API period should not accumulate stall debt) AND (b) fix the comment to be accurate. Note the subtlety: with (a), during an outage the budget check still fires (budget is independent) — correct, the budget remains the backstop. 

Where exactly: in the error branch:

```bash
if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
 status="error/-"
 running=""
fi
``

But careful: `now=$(date +%s)` is computed AFTER the completed-check, and the refresh uses `$now`. The error branch runs BEFORE `now` exists for this iteration. Options: refresh with the timestamp captured later — restructure: move the error handling after `now=$(date +%s)`, or set a flag. Let me look at the current code:

```bash
   observed="$(gh run view ...)" || observed=""
   status="${observed%% *}"
   running="${observed##* }"
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     status="error/-"
     running=""
   fi
   if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
   now=$(date +%s)
   # comment...
   wedge=""
   if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
     wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
   elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
     last_running="$now"
   elif ...
``

Simplest correct change: in the error branch, don't have `now` yet — but `date +%s` is cheap; I can set `now=$(date +%s)` inside the error branch before refreshing, and then the later `now=$(date +%s)` re-captures (fine, same second typically; slightly later is fine too). OR restructure: capture `now` right after the parse, before the completed check — but `now` is only needed when not completed; capturing always is harmless (one extra date call per poll — negligible vs the gh call). Cleanest: set `now=$(date +%s)` BEFORE the completed check? That changes the semantic slightly (now includes the view-call duration — already does). Actually simplest minimal diff honoring the reviewer's snippet: inside the error branch:

```bash
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     # API unreachable — no signal, no stall accumulation (review: an
     # outage outliving the window must not false-wedge a healthy child;
     # the budget stays the backstop). Cannot observe = cannot judge.
     status="error/-"
     running=""
     last_running="$(date +%s)"
   fi
``

Wait — but then the comment block before the wedge chain mentions "An empty poll (failed call) counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip." — reword per (b): "A failed poll is 'cannot observe': it refreshes the stall clock (no signal, no accumulation) — an outage outliving the window is not treated as a child stall; the budget remains the backstop. (A single blip neither trips nor accumulates.)"

Hmm, one nuance: refreshing last_running on error polls means a MISBEHAVING gh (persistent failures) never trips the stall — only the budget catches it. That's exactly what the reviewer wants ("cannot observe = cannot judge", "the containment action is moot anyway: gh run cancel hits the same unavailable API"). ✓

TDD: RED test — a test where the stub's view calls fail for a stretch LONGER than the stall window while the child is quiet... but "quiet" (running=0) can't be observed if ALL view calls fail. The false-wedge scenario: last successful poll saw running=0 (clock started), then N failed polls spanning > window, then a successful poll sees the child healthy (running=1 or completes). With CURRENT code: the stall check at the first post-outage successful poll: elapsed (now - last_running) > window → false wedge. With FIX: error polls refreshed the clock → no wedge.

Test design:
- DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3, DW_POLL_SECONDS=0 (fast spins; error polls spin rapidly — each failed call consumes nothing), budget must be > total time or exactly controlled.
- Stub needs an error-injection fixture: e.g. `view-error-calls` file containing a NUMBER of initial view calls to fail (exit 1 / empty output). Add stub support: if `$GH_STUB_DIR/view-fail-next` exists with count N > 0, decrement and exit 1 (empty output, like a real gh network failure). The script: `observed="" || ...` → error path.

Timeline (poll=0, stall=3):
- poll1 (success): view 'in_progress -', jobs '0' → running=0 → clock=last_running=t0. 
- polls 2..k (FAIL, 4+ seconds): each refreshes clock with fix; without fix, clock stays t0.
- poll k+1 (success): 'in_progress -', jobs '1' (running job! healthy child resumed) → with fix: running=1 → refresh, no wedge → continue → next poll completes success → exit 0. Without fix: running=1 → the elif chain: running>0 → REFRESH branch (no wedge check!!) — wait, if the post-outage poll reports running=1, the wedge never evaluates (running>0 refreshes) — NOT RED.

Hmm. For the current code to false-wedge, the first successful poll after the outage must report running=0 AND elapsed > window: then `elif running==0 && elapsed > stall` → wedge. So: after the outage, the successful poll sees jobs '0' again, THEN the child picks up: next success poll sees '1', then completes. Without fix: wedge at the first post-outage quiet poll. With fix: no wedge; the quiet-post-outage poll's elapsed = 0 (clock just refreshed by the last error poll... wait — with the fix, the last error poll set last_running≈t_k; the first success poll at t_k(+ε): running=0 → elapsed ~0 < 3 ✓ no wedge; then jobs '1' → refresh; then completed → exit 0 ✓.

Timing: need the failed-poll stretch to span > stall (3s) for RED. Error polls with sleep=0 spin fast (each ~ms) — thousands of polls in 3s — fine, but for the clock to EXCEED the window without the fix, real wall time must pass: the stretch of failed polls must last > 3s wall. Options: DW_POLL_SECONDS applies to `sleep $poll` at the END of the loop iteration — error polls DO sleep poll seconds each iteration (the sleep is at the bottom, unconditional). So DW_POLL_SECONDS=2 with, say, 3 failed polls → outage spans ~4-6s > 3 ✓. Then success poll. Total runtime ~6-8s. Margins: without fix, the post-outage success poll at t≈6: elapsed 6 > 3 ✓ wedge (RED, margin 3s). With fix: clock refreshed at t≈4 (last error poll), success poll t≈6: elapsed 2 < 3 ✓ no wedge (margin 1s) — acceptable; widen: poll=2, 4 failed polls (t≈8), stall=5: RED: 8 > 5 ✓ margin 3; GREEN: last error at t≈8, success at t≈8-10 → elapsed ≤2 < 5 ✓ margin 3. Then jobs '1' poll, then completed poll. Budget: 60 (never fires). Runtime ~12s (6 polls × 2s). Fine.

Wait — also ensure the FIRST poll (before outage) is success+quiet: sets baseline clock. Fixtures: view-111: 'in_progress -' ×5 then 'completed success' (repeats last when exhausted). jobs-111: '0\n' (baseline), then error polls consume nothing (stub exits before serving), then '0\n' (post-outage quiet), '1\n' (running), then completed poll consumes whatever (last repeats). Let me count stub consumption: stub fails BEFORE touching fixtures when fail-next>0.

view-111.txt: poll1→'in_progress -'; polls2-5 fail; poll6→'…

  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"

New lap: 1 open SUGESTION thread on my own pushed code (`scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh:158`):

**Finding**: An error poll (empty `observed`) sets `running=""`, which skips BOTH the refresh branch and the stall branch — so `last_running` stays at the last *successful* poll and the stall clock keeps accumulating during an API outage. A sustained outage (> stall window, ~31m on testflight) that starts while the child is quiet false-wedges a healthy child. Also the comment "counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip" overstates — it's "neither refreshes nor trips".

Reviewer offers two tightenings, either alone suffices:
(a) refresh `last_running="$now"` on error polls too ("cannot observe = cannot judge"), and/or
(b) reword the comment to match the accepted-residual-class framing.

While it says "no urgency — fold into a follow-up or leave as documented debt", the rework rules say every open thread needs a code fix in this pass. Best response: implement (a) — it's the materially safer behavior (an unobservable API period should not accumulate stall debt) AND (b) fix the comment to be accurate. Note the subtlety: with (a), during an outage the budget check still fires (budget is independent) — correct, the budget remains the backstop. 

Where exactly: in the error branch:

```bash
if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
 status="error/-"
 running=""
fi
``

But careful: `now=$(date +%s)` is computed AFTER the completed-check, and the refresh uses `$now`. The error branch runs BEFORE `now` exists for this iteration. Options: refresh with the timestamp captured later — restructure: move the error handling after `now=$(date +%s)`, or set a flag. Let me look at the current code:

```bash
   observed="$(gh run view ...)" || observed=""
   status="${observed%% *}"
   running="${observed##* }"
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     status="error/-"
     running=""
   fi
   if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
   now=$(date +%s)
   # comment...
   wedge=""
   if [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
     wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
   elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
     last_running="$now"
   elif ...
``

Simplest correct change: in the error branch, don't have `now` yet — but `date +%s` is cheap; I can set `now=$(date +%s)` inside the error branch before refreshing, and then the later `now=$(date +%s)` re-captures (fine, same second typically; slightly later is fine too). OR restructure: capture `now` right after the parse, before the completed check — but `now` is only needed when not completed; capturing always is harmless (one extra date call per poll — negligible vs the gh call). Cleanest: set `now=$(date +%s)` BEFORE the completed check? That changes the semantic slightly (now includes the view-call duration — already does). Actually simplest minimal diff honoring the reviewer's snippet: inside the error branch:

```bash
   if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "$status" = "$observed" ]; then
     # API unreachable — no signal, no stall accumulation (review: an
     # outage outliving the window must not false-wedge a healthy child;
     # the budget stays the backstop). Cannot observe = cannot judge.
     status="error/-"
     running=""
     last_running="$(date +%s)"
   fi
``

Wait — but then the comment block before the wedge chain mentions "An empty poll (failed call) counts as progress: never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip." — reword per (b): "A failed poll is 'cannot observe': it refreshes the stall clock (no signal, no accumulation) — an outage outliving the window is not treated as a child stall; the budget remains the backstop. (A single blip neither trips nor accumulates.)"

Hmm, one nuance: refreshing last_running on error polls means a MISBEHAVING gh (persistent failures) never trips the stall — only the budget catches it. That's exactly what the reviewer wants ("cannot observe = cannot judge", "the containment action is moot anyway: gh run cancel hits the same unavailable API"). ✓

TDD: RED test — a test where the stub's view calls fail for a stretch LONGER than the stall window while the child is quiet... but "quiet" (running=0) can't be observed if ALL view calls fail. The false-wedge scenario: last successful poll saw running=0 (clock started), then N failed polls spanning > window, then a successful poll sees the child healthy (running=1 or completes). With CURRENT code: the stall check at the first post-outage successful poll: elapsed (now - last_running) > window → false wedge. With FIX: error polls refreshed the clock → no wedge.

Test design:
- DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3, DW_POLL_SECONDS=0 (fast spins; error polls spin rapidly — each failed call consumes nothing), budget must be > total time or exactly controlled.
- Stub needs an error-injection fixture: e.g. `view-error-calls` file containing a NUMBER of initial view calls to fail (exit 1 / empty output). Add stub support: if `$GH_STUB_DIR/view-fail-next` exists with count N > 0, decrement and exit 1 (empty output, like a real gh network failure). The script: `observed="" || ...` → error path.

Timeline (poll=0, stall=3):
- poll1 (success): view 'in_progress -', jobs '0' → running=0 → clock=last_running=t0. 
- polls 2..k (FAIL, 4+ seconds): each refreshes clock with fix; without fix, clock stays t0.
- poll k+1 (success): 'in_progress -', jobs '1' (running job! healthy child resumed) → with fix: running=1 → refresh, no wedge → continue → next poll completes success → exit 0. Without fix: running=1 → the elif chain: running>0 → REFRESH branch (no wedge check!!) — wait, if the post-outage poll reports running=1, the wedge never evaluates (running>0 refreshes) — NOT RED.

Hmm. For the current code to false-wedge, the first successful poll after the outage must report running=0 AND elapsed > window: then `elif running==0 && elapsed > stall` → wedge. So: after the outage, the successful poll sees jobs '0' again, THEN the child picks up: next success poll sees '1', then completes. Without fix: wedge at the first post-outage quiet poll. With fix: no wedge; the quiet-post-outage poll's elapsed = 0 (clock just refreshed by the last error poll... wait — with the fix, the last error poll set last_running≈t_k; the first success poll at t_k(+ε): running=0 → elapsed ~0 < 3 ✓ no wedge; then jobs '1' → refresh; then completed → exit 0 ✓.

Timing: need the failed-poll stretch to span > stall (3s) for RED. - **New bug found while fixing the BLOCKING thread** (the fixture inertness was hiding it): with a *live* jobs feed, the PR's `elif` chain made the **budget check unreachable** (it sat behind the running-job refresh branch), so the watcher spun **forever** on a healthy child that outlived the budget — reproduced at 500+ polls with no self-heal. The #344 budget self-heal only ever fired because the broken stub always reported 0 running jobs. Fixed: the budget check is evaluated **first**; the gh-172 stall check remains the fast path for the quiet zombie.
- Standing ops note from the PR unchanged: the physical `fa-m5-1` worker still needs reboot/de-register; the guard only bounds leg damage and surfaces the signature in the leg log.

## Approach

- **Thread 1 (BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub, vacuous transient test)** — TDD:
  - *RED*: kept the broken `seq -f` body construction while adding the new assertions — 3 tests failed exactly as the reviewer predicted (served bodies `['', …]`, no refresh coverage).
  - *GREEN*: stub body built with the suggested pipeline — `seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -` (`n=0` → `{"jobs":[]}`); the stub now appends the **body it actually served** to `jobs-served-<id>.log`, and the tests assert it — an inert fixture can never pass again. The "absent file = 1 job always running" contract is now true **and asserted**.
  - The transient test is re-timed so the refresh path is genuinely exercised: poll 1 quiet (3s) → poll 2 **running** (3s) → poll 3 quiet → poll 4 completes, window 5s, budget 60. Poll 3 stays under the window **only** if poll 2 refreshed `last_running`. *Mutation-verified*: disabling `last_running="$now"` turns the test red (`exit 0` → `exit 1`, cancel + re-dispatch in the log); the reviewer's "green with a deliberately broken guard" repro is dead.
- **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT — fixed 600s window false-wedges sibling-queued children)** — options (b)+(c):
  - Default is now `max(600, budget/8)` when `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` is unset (testflight 15000s → 1875s ≈ 31m; addin 3600s → 600s floor).
  - The effective window is echoed on the `watching …` line (`(queue-stall window Ns)`) for leg-log diagnostics, and pinned by a new test: floor (`800` → `600s`), scaled (`16000` → `2000s`); the queue-stall test asserts the explicit override still wins (`queue-stall window 1s`).
  - The false "A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the real contention analysis (cli `build-macos` matrix vs testflight's pinned jobs on `fa-m5-1`; hosted queue crunches), and the **accepted residual class** (sibling occupancy > budget/8 can still false-wedge into the one self-heal — bounded, diagnosed, inside the leg ceiling) is documented in the script header + `queue_stall` comment.
  - `daily-publish.yml` gh-172 arithmetic updated: second-wedge fail-fast worst case testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m stall = 294m < 360m.
- **Thread 3 (SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` per poll)**: the watch loop issues a single `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call; status/conclusion and the running count parse from one jq line (`… + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)`). Halves per-poll traffic and makes the two-call completion race structurally impossible; a failed call still counts as progress (blip tolerance preserved). The stub serves the combined call from `view-<id>.txt` + `jobs-<id>.txt` consumed in lockstep, still piping through the **real jq expression**, and the transient test pins **4 `run view` invocations for 4 polls** (the two-call shape made 8).

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — budget-first wedge ordering (+ the bug comment); merged single `gh run view` call per poll; `queue_stall` default `max(600, budget/8)` with honest contention/residual-class docs; window echoed on the `watching` line; header + env-knob docs updated.
